DROP_SNAPSHOT_ROW … }) — the seed is a FILTERED synthetic snapshot, so table- and row-level dropping at the cut already exists as a mechanism.\n\nRULING: (1) The scanner (WI-4419 no-path-exclude; WI-37553 owner-authorised machine label ONLY) is CORRECT and stays as is — no acceptance widening, no path exclude. P-201 stays blocked-by P-504.\n4. Recorded here instead of narrowing the item text so the item's intent (no leg skipped) is preserved; the stale 'Blocked on EI-21848848412437329' note on that item is su-55a5b's to fix (that EI is done).\nRelated: P-201, P-302, P-504","date":"2026-09-02","itemRefs":["P-008","P-201","P-302","P-504"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":339},{"id":"D-005","title":"P-504 root cause: fix the backfill enqueue predicate in operator-core, not the release caller or the flag","body":"Date: 2026-09-02\nP-504 (WI-2141185) is root-caused. The tower federation storm is NOT primarily a rejoin effect: it is the **nightly release seed cut**, recurring daily at 07:00Z (`bin/release-local.sh <ver> nightly` → `cut-seed-quiesced.sh:106` → `cut-seed-cli --workspace-id`, no `--no-force-backfill`). Confirmed by su-0300e: their 07:03–07:15Z P-004 sample ran no cut.\n\n**Mechanism.** `backfillLocalState` exists to rescue rows that predate the capture trigger and so never fired it — that condition is `fed_ts IS NULL`. The enqueue SELECTs never expressed it; they selected every local row. So the per-target `backfill_done` marker was the ONLY idempotence guard, and `force` bypasses exactly that marker. `force` therefore meant \"re-enqueue the entire projection\". It also skips `markTargetDone`, so nothing records the sweep and every forced run repeats it in full. cut-seed-cli passes `force:true, maxOpsPerAuthor:0` — the latter sets the per-author budget to Infinity, and `force` also skips the 1000-row bail cap (gated on `!opts.force`). Every guard is off at once.\n\n**Measured 2026-09-02** (live corpus, old predicate vs new): engineer_issues 149,372→0 · harness_plans 1,625→0 · harness_features_consolidated 1,238→0 · plan_item_assignments 98→0 · pot_members 2→0. **152,335 rows re-enqueued per nightly cut, of which 0 genuinely needed it.** The running cut has been blocked since 07:06Z logging `[cut-seed] waiting for the operator to drain N outbox row(s)` every 5s — waiting on the backlog it created. That backlog is why coordination rows federate ~6h late.\n\n**DECISION — the fix goes in `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/backfill-local-state.ts`, at the predicate.** Add the missing `fed_ts IS NULL` condition to both enqueue paths and both candidate counts, plus an explicit `resyncFederated` option for a deliberate re-anchor. Consequences other lanes must follow:\n\n1. **Do NOT fix this by passing `--no-force-backfill`** in the release step. That flag makes the marker authoritative, and the marker is dated 2026-06-25 — it would skip engineer_issues wholesale. It trades a flood for a staleness risk and leaves the defect armed for every other caller. The predicate fix makes `force` cheap and correct, so the release caller needs no change at all.\n2. **The release path stays untouched**, so the `apps/operator/lib/release/**` human policy gate (D-003) does not apply to this fix. That gate is why EI-12727 — the same defect, filed 2026-07-15 from the corestore-ratchet angle — was parked `needs-human` on 2026-08-21. It was parked for the wrong path; the defect is in operator-core, which is not gated.\n3. **Seed completeness is preserved.** Genuinely-unfederated rows are still enqueued, which is the constraint EI-12727's reviewer flagged as non-negotiable.\n4. **EI-12727 is the same defect and should close against this landing**, not separately. It is the earlier and better-measured report (237→335 MiB corestore ratchet per cut, +8,150 appends). In July the sweep was 8,170 rows; engineer_issues alone is now ~150k, which is why an installer-size annoyance became a coordination outage.\n\n**Not decided here:** P-504(d) drain priority/ordering. That changes shared drain behavior and needs its own decision before anyone touches it.","date":"2026-09-02","itemRefs":["P-504","P-004"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":352},{"id":"D-006","title":"Re-pin the witness candidate past the P-203 zombie-eviction fix: build #7 from staging 531fcc2863 (or any later staging commit); P-302 verdicts taken at the D-159 pin 5be66dc6 stay valid","body":"Date: 2026-09-02\nRULING. The repacked 5be66dc6 .deb (/tmp/p101-build/p302-gate.deb) may finish its current local-matrix run and be banked as P-302 evidence; it is NOT reused for any escalation-sensitive leg.\n\nWHY NOT WAIT FOR A GREEN. The routine `nightly-release-cut` (install papercusp, cron '0 0 3 * * *' = 07:00Z, next fire 2026-09-03T07:00Z) is paused via routines:set until BOTH WI-2141185 fixes are in green main: a666841c (backfill-local-state.ts fed_ts predicate, mechanism 2) and b83535c9 (hive-membership-admission.ts once-per-process re-grant, mechanism 1). Un-pause condition: `git merge-base --is-ancestor a666841c main && git merge-base --is-ancestor b83535c9 main` both true (ancestry is sufficient here because the question is 'does the nightly's cut source carry the fix', and the cut source IS main^{commit}).\n\nWHY. nightly-release-cut-action.ts resolves sourceSha = `git rev-parse main^{commit}` of the integration root, materializes /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp-nightly-release at that sha (setup-release-checkout.sh --ref) and runs that checkout's release-local.sh, whose cut-seed-quiesced.sh --workspace-id path calls backfillLocalState force:true — the exact producer of today's 07:03:33Z re-capture of ~142k already-federated engineer_issues rows (WI-2141185 mechanism 2; head-of-line blocks ALL federation incl. coord_event_log for ~20h, EI-22138988923269437). main is a2d69cef (2026-08-20, the last green) and the gate is frozen on 797454468a with 91 consecutive reds, so main will not carry either fix by tomorrow's fire without two green runs. Nothing is lost by pausing: today's nightly cut-seed already FAILED at 08:18:31Z ('NO progress draining 146295 outbox rows in 810s') and would fail the same way tonight while ALSO re-flooding the outbox. The pause is a deliberate hold visible as `paused` in routines:list (distinct from a stall); the owner can lift it any time with routines:set.\n\nMeasured: routines:list q:'nightly' → nightly-release-cut cron '0 0 3 * * *' active=true nextFireAt 2026-09-03T07:00:00Z lastFiredAt 2026-09-02T07:00:45Z paused=null (before this ruling). packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/nightly-release-cut-action.ts:241 `execFileSync('git', ['-C', sourceRoot, 'rev-parse', 'main^{commit}'])`; :142 the managed argv runs setup-release-checkout.sh --ref \"$PAPERCUSP_EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA\" then `bin/release-local.sh \"$1\" nightly` inside the release checkout. `git -C …/papercusp-nightly-release log -1` → a2d69cef50 2026-08-20T16:15:14-04:00 'Repair frozen candidate f9030aa73955' = `git rev-parse --short main`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor a666841c main` → NOT in main; same for b83535c9. dev:pipeline_position: gate consecutiveReds=91, repairQueue candidate 797454468a phase ready-to-test, lastGreen a2d69cef. journalctl 08:18:31Z cut-seed FAILED (carry check #nightly-dead).\nRelated: P-504, P-201","date":"2026-09-02","itemRefs":["P-504","P-201"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":380},{"id":"D-008","title":"Phase-6 code evidence PASSES at the pinned candidate on RE-MEASURED greens, not the original ones — and P-401 must name which RELEASE-READINESS.md version it signs","body":"Date: 2026-09-02\nDate: 2026-09-02. Do not re-raise them as fabricated citations.\n\nThree changes are genuinely independent and post-green:\n- P-509 `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/hive-epoch-boot-deps.ts` — 30d2acec25, 2026-08-31T17:00:45Z (+5d), +8/-1\n- P-510 `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts` and `index.test.ts` — 2c9612c603, 2026-09-01T01:19:22Z (+5d), +10/-4 and +4\n- P-507 `.../projections/__tests__/explicit-provenance-contract.test.ts` — 9d97c73279 (08-28) **+58 assertions**, then 5543d15230 (08-30) −9/+1\n\nP-507 is the sharp one: its green was reported as \"84/84\", and the contract test that green rests on subsequently grew by 58 assertions. The original pass cannot have covered them. P-511's bar — \"a stale green ... is NO-GO\" — was met on its face.\n\n#### 2. RULING: the staleness is retired BY MEASUREMENT, not waived.\nMeasured: `testing:run` runIds `21ac9bab-038d-41e6-86c8-0dd769dfbd04` (55/55, 4 files) and `61b3697f-e648-45fc-97b9-56ec50368279` (87/87, 2 files) = **142/142 pass, 0 failures, 0 collection failures**.\n\nAdmissibility, because `test:file` runs the WORKING TREE and a green there proves nothing about the candidate on its own:\n- `git status --porcelain` scoped to all 13 paths returned ZERO lines — the run measured COMMITTED blobs, not a peer's uncommitted edit.\n- Blob-compared candidate vs staging for all 13: **12 of 13 CANDIDATE_EQ_STAGING**, so for every code and test path the executed content is byte-identical to the candidate's.\n\nPhase-6 CODE evidence therefore PASSES at the pinned candidate. The current generation is only a hash of hive+repo; production passes a local pot slug and receiver state is read from a namespace overwritten by fetch.\n\nImplementation ruling under D-016: signed hive identity is the existing hive public key, repo identity remains canonicalRepoKey, and generation is per signing device's physical bare-store incarnation. A local-only Git marker identifies the physical store; the existing git-sync routine metadata allocates a monotonic generation ordinal that survives store recreation. The signed generation ID carries ordinal+incarnation; sequence restarts in the new generation. Receivers compare generation first, then sequence, never arrival time. A valid signature cannot revive an older generation or substitute a nonce at an already-used ordinal.\n\nPersist accepted peer snapshot floors in existing routine metadata, separate from fetch-overwritable namespace refs. Only a verified, scoped, reconciled fetched snapshot may advance those floors. Strict runtime readers reject unnegotiated legacy envelopes, bind staging to the same stable scope, and preserve the independent authority epoch/sequence fence. P-514 consumes this context instead of reconstructing a second identity source. This extends existing Git and routine-state surfaces; no new transport, database table or service.\nRelated: P-513, P-514, P-521","date":"2026-09-05","itemRefs":["P-514","P-513","P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":568},{"id":"D-022","title":"F6 uses the owning hive key as a single authority; membership elections grant no exclusive effects","body":"Date: 2026-09-05\nMeasured: 2026-09-05T17:07Z. Read identity/hive-keypair.ts, integrator-tick.ts/integrator.ts, staging-advance.ts/worktree-bridge.ts, github-bridge-tick.ts/github-egress.ts/github-fork-egress.ts, release-promotion.ts and git-sync-action.ts production call sites. The hive private key already lives only on the owning Swarm; joined views hold its public identity. Existing Git integration/egress relies on local presence selection and FF/CAS, which cannot grant exclusive cross-machine authority.\n\nF6 implementation uses the explicitly permitted SINGLE authority model, extending the existing hive signing identity rather than adding a quorum/election service. Only the owning hive key may authorize canonical integration, release promotion, and automatic GitHub publication/fork-PR effects. Git sinks require a fresh operation-bound owner proof immediately before mutation; canonical staging announcements carry an owner countersignature verified by receivers against their pinned hive/repository context. This is Phase G of the physical drill (runbook row G / P-308), and the evidence goes on P-521's work-item. P-521 must not close without it. Rationale: same as D-036. The rig is single-custody (P-203) and only the integrated F1-F8 candidate makes a packaged sink proof meaningful. Keeping P-517 open would recreate the P-517<->P-521 dependency cycle. It would be refused, and a second build of the same sha would compete with the nightly for disk and CPU.\n2. D-040(3) still holds: this same build is the VM post-fold build.\n3. OWNER WALL: two things need release:cut op:run, which is owner-walled. P-521 does not claim 'reproducible' until one of those runs, or until the owner rules the nightly acceptable as the journey artifact.\n4. These build cuts should always come from the latest green main unless explicitly said otherwise\" (spacing normalized). The recorded decline concerns duplicate execution by that source session, not withdrawal of the release request. D-067 selects the alpha cut; D-068 adds the link-join eligibility requirement; D-070 assigns desktop cut/publication to e33a454a and P2P acceptance to 97bcc752.\n\nRuling:\n1. For the final 0.0.22 alpha/P-521 cut, select the latest GREEN main tip at a recorded final source-decision timestamp immediately before launch. If several eligible green revisions exist, use the newest tip then. This explicitly supersedes D-068 rule 1's FIRST-green selection wording; its earliest-eligible threshold does not reserve an older commit against Avi's latest-green instruction.\n2. Eligibility is unchanged: retain promotion evidence for that exact 40-character SHA; verify the D-040/D-068 required fixes and packaging repairs WI-10003271/EI-24350216350047928. Show fix ancestry where applicable, or exact equivalent blob/patch containment for admitted/cherry-picked repairs, and verify the candidate's joined_via_link behavior (WI-10003277), not merely the fix's presence on staging. If the latest green tip is not eligible, wait for an eligible latest tip; do not silently select an older source or widen eligibility.\n3. Record that timestamp, immutable SHA, promotion reference and source/behavior evidence before launch. Once that cut starts, freeze this SHA for all build legs, seed/provenance, manifest and candidate acceptance. A subsequent main advance does not retarget an in-flight cut or justify mixing artifacts. A new/restarted cut after abandoning an attempt requires a new recorded prelaunch selection; a same-attempt recovery must preserve its frozen source and provenance.\n4. D-067's seed/boot/platform/provenance conditions, D-068's exclusion of fixless shakedown evidence, D-070 custody, physical journeys, independent GO and the real 72-hour soak remain unchanged. This decision names no currently eligible SHA, authorizes no gate operation, and grants no exemption from release preflight.\n\nRationale: honor Avi's latest-green rule at the actual launch boundary while giving the build and acceptance one stable artifact lineage.\nRelated: P-202, P-203, P-501, P-521","date":"2026-09-26","itemRefs":["P-521","P-202","P-203","P-501"],"affects":["desktop-0022-operator-release-recovery-2026-09-25"],"lineNumber":988},{"id":"D-072","title":"P-202 closes on current-build live two-host evidence (VM 587f459be598); the final-artifact re-proof rides P-521","body":"Date: 2026-09-27\nDate: 2026-09-27. su-3ee17ad9, AUTO under owner directive #714 (carry of #708), whole-plan driver WI-2037678.\n\nMEASURED 15:28-15:30Z on the physical rig (tower + Mac VM, rig lock fad7421e), VM operator build 587f459be598, with harness shipped in the payload (WI-10003486):\n- claude seat opus/high, run 15:28Z (task 0mujz3r2kek9kbxaqgw): PASS=7 FAIL=0 SKIP=2. WD-5 gave a pre-boot refused:agent_runtime_missing (codex is not installed on the VM) and spent no seats; the refusal is origin-observable.\n- WD-8 meter is SKIP (recordSpendDurable is unbuilt; out of v1 per the plan note on WorkOffer+meter). WD-9 revocation is SKIP by construction (the fed_reap matrix covers it).\n\nThe three defects that held WD-5/WD-6 red today are fixed and verified live: WI-10003468 (codex seats launched as claude), WI-10003470 (stale builtin su.mode-auto broke the mode catalog) and WI-10003486 (the rig payload read the installed 0.0.19 harness). WI-10003427 (bg-host merge-apply freeze) had already unblocked WD-2.\n\nRULING: P-202's acceptance gap was a LIVE headless-honor boot/run, and it is now proven on the current build, which is the default non-final acceptance plane. P-202 moves to done. Final-release evidence on the exact shipped artifact is NOT inferred from this: D-068 already requires the final P-521 candidate to pass P-202, so that re-run belongs to P-521 on the pinned candidate.\n\nOpen, non-blocking: WI-10003481 (a tower log admitted after its connection opens gets no replicator; mitigated by a VM kickstart) is still wip.","date":"2026-09-27","itemRefs":["P-202","P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1005},{"id":"D-073","title":"P-203 closes on current-build live two-host pot-git + substrate convergence (tower + Mac VM, VM build fc5dbddfb2c8); the final-artifact re-proof rides P-521","body":"Date: 2026-09-27\nDate: 2026-09-27. su-3ee17ad9, AUTO, carrying this plan (WI-2037678). This applies the D-072 pattern (P-202) to P-203.\nRULING: Leg A storage+join is PROVEN on current build. The P-521 integrated hardened-artifact acceptance re-runs the physical journeys on the exact release artifact, so a pinned-build re-proof here would duplicate P-521 without adding evidence. The pot-git convergence half was the open RED (WI-2142873) and is now green.\nEVIDENCE (measured 2026-09-27):\n- Substrate: VM LIVE-ALL at 19:26:24Z shows 39/39 logs notConverged=0. The tower merge cursor for VM log f8987962 advanced 16347 -> 19125 (19:25:55Z).\n- pot-git VM->tower: VM convergence at 19:21:31Z converged (judged=1 non-self peer, behindCount=0); at 19:31:28Z trailing healthy (XPAsvso1 local v2937 < announced v2940, 0m without progress). XPAsvso1 floor went none -> v2926 -> v2940.\n- pot-git tower->VM: tower convergence at 19:34:34Z trailing healthy (dcJWGlbQ local v6 < announced v7). The earlier 19:24Z NOT CONVERGED on v3<v5 cleared after the tower fetched v5 at 19:25:05Z (the VM had been redeploying).\n- Worktree bridge accepted 94 = consumed 94, acceptFreeTicks 0. Own-head publish changed=true, refused=null, backlogRemains=false.\n- Since the VM's 19:20:39Z restart: 0 receive-fetch failures, 0 NOT CONVERGED, 0 publish-guard refusals.\nFixes behind the green: WI-2142873 (ref-announce newer-snapshot acceptance), WI-10003481, WI-10003506, WI-10003527, WI-10003529, WI-10003528, plus the worktree-bridge timeout/reclaim and own-head shallow-coverage fixes.\nNOT covered and still open: EI-24442974511093259. This does not affect pot-git publish or convergence and is a hygiene/design follow-up.\nConsequence: P-204 (Leg E) is unblocked. P-521's remaining unresolved blocker becomes P-204.","date":"2026-09-27","itemRefs":["P-202","P-203","P-521","P-007","P-204"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1020},{"id":"D-074","title":"P-521 needs a fresh alpha cut from green main: neither published 0.0.22-alpha nor the 0.0.23 Windows hotfix carries WI-10003277","body":"Date: 2026-09-28\nDate: 2026-09-28\nsu-3ee17ad9, AUTO under owner directive #801, whole-plan driver WI-2037678. Amends the cut-custody half of D-069/D-070 and applies D-068/D-071.\n\nMEASURED 17:20Z (git rev-parse <tag>:packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/federation-scope.ts):\n- desktop-v0.0.22-alpha -> 7708e704, blob 169eabc650 (the pre-fix blob named in D-068)\n- desktop-v0.0.23-alpha (Windows-only hotfix, 0.0.22 source + papercusp-desktop 1ad0099559) -> 851fcfbe, blob 169eabc650\n- desktop-v0.0.22-20260928.0701-nightly -> 09e39c5d, blob 169eabc650\n- main 01a67545 and staging -> blob ce463464 (carries WI-10003277)\n\nWhat happened: owner #735 ('cut a new 0.0.22 release off of our latest green main') was executed by su-cc07079c from 7708e704 and published. Per owner #800, Linux/macOS stay at 0.0.22 and the Windows 0.0.23 hotfix shows inside the same card (WI-10003687, live 16:29Z). That satisfies owner #85's cut-and-publish ask behind WI-10002423, so WI-10002423 is NOT re-cut or force-claimed. su-e33a454a never picked up the 16:46Z wake, and the item is unassigned.\n\nRULING:\n1. Per D-068, no artifact published today can be the P-521 candidate.\n2. The P-521 candidate is a fresh LOCAL alpha cut (release:cut, artifacts stay local; owner uploads) from the latest eligible green main at recorded prelaunch time. Its exact source is frozen per D-071, and the cut must carry the ce463464-or-later federation-scope blob. The version defaults to 0.0.24-alpha: 0.0.22 and 0.0.23 are taken, and the updater needs monotonic versions. [inferred default, disclosed; owner may override] The alpha build type follows the owner's D-067 answer.\n3. SEQUENCING: the macOS build leg runs on the same Mac VM as the hive-git physical rig, where /Volumes/BuildData holds both the build data and the rig's PG. So the cut launches only after P-505 run 15 (P-204 Leg E) finishes and the hive-git-physical-rig lease is released. It also must not collide with su-cc07079c's interrupted Linux+Windows op ac651888, whose Linux 0.0.23 bytes are intentionally unpublished; that op is resolved or abandoned first.\n4. Cut custody for P-521 moves to the whole-plan driver (su-3ee17ad9) under WI-10002524. su-97bcc752 (D-070) and su-e33a454a are no longer live on it.\n\nNot changed: every P-521 acceptance condition (physical journeys on the exact artifact, computed manifest, independent non-implementer GO).","date":"2026-09-28","itemRefs":["P-521","P-505","P-204"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1034},{"id":"D-075","title":"P-521 candidate must also carry WI-10003731 (pot integrator host-local state fix); cut waits for green main containing it","body":"Date: 2026-09-28\nDate: 2026-09-28\nsu-3ee17ad9, AUTO under owner directive #801, whole-plan driver WI-2037678. Amends D-074 point 2 (source eligibility). Applies D-068/D-071.\n\nMEASURED:\n- Root cause (WI-10003731): harness_escalations was sync:'git', so every pot device's git-sync committed its own per-host watchdog output (.papercusp/state/escalations/<phase>.md) into the shared pot repo. Each member head then content-conflicted against staging, and the integrator parked it. hello-world-3-pot staging sat at dd578ec5 from 2026-09-27 00:23Z while the VM head ba9ce0fb waited, with integrator_status 'no advance (conflicts=1)'.\n- Fix (committed on staging, 0d5858e9 and neighbours): table-registry.ts retires harness_escalations to sync:'none'. integrator.ts re-merges with -X ours when EVERY conflicted path is retired host-local state, and parks otherwise, naming the paths.\n- Live on the tower (bg-host MainPID 1691737, restarted 18:32:09Z): the 18:40:02Z tick advanced staging to 69c6ccc, which has parents dd578ec + ba9ce0f and subject 'integrate 75c2561a56d0 @ ba9ce0fb (host-local state kept from staging: ...escalations/github-bridge.md, ...escalations/origin-freshness-watchdog.md)'.\n\nRULING:\n1. The released artifact runs the same git-export and integrator code, so without this fix every multi-device pot stops integrating as soon as its hosts' watchdog output diverges. That is a P2P correctness blocker. The P-521 candidate must carry the WI-10003731 integrator.ts + table-registry.ts blobs, as well as the ce463464-or-later federation-scope blob from D-074.\n2. Eligibility is still 'latest eligible green main at recorded prelaunch time' (D-071). A green main that lacks WI-10003731 is NOT eligible. The cut therefore waits until the green-checkpoint promotes a staging commit that carries the fix. The gate lane stays with its owner; this plan does not do LIVE_GATE_OPS for it.\n3. I re-acquired the rig at 19:26Z and sent a correction (msg muln159e).\n\nNot changed: every P-521 acceptance condition.","date":"2026-09-28","itemRefs":["P-505","P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1072},{"id":"D-077","title":"Admitted GitHub-origin heads integrate through the bridge's P-005 admission, not the G-5c device-tier gate (WI-10003820)","body":"Date: 2026-09-29\nContext: P-505 run 31 (2026-09-29) Phase E showed that on a bridged hive the GitHub bridge ingressed and admitted a fresh upstream commit (last_admitted=140b4edc), but canonical staging never moved. No production code fed the admitted github-origin head to the integrator. collectGateableHeads reads only attested member devices with accepted signed ref-announce floors, and the synthetic github-origin device has no keypair, no sigrefs and no comms tier.\n\nDecision [self-imposed, AUTO under owner #801]: runIntegratorTick takes an explicit admittedGithubOriginHead input. runIntegratorLeg fills it from routines.metadata.github_bridge.last_admitted, the admission watermark written by the bridge leg earlier in the same tick, keyed by githubOriginNamespaceKey(entry.github_remote). The head skips the sigrefs floor and the G-5c tier gate: P-005 admission (revocation over lastAdmitted..head) is its gate, as github-ingress.ts S-3 specifies. Only the admitted watermark is fed, never the raw namespace head, so an ingressed-but-blocked commit stays out. A head whose object is absent from the store is reported and skipped.\n\nConsequence: a PR merged on GitHub now reaches canonical staging on the next bridged tick and is egressed to the fork on the tick after. Rejected alternative: routing the github-origin head through the G-5c ratification queue. It would park every GitHub-side commit for owner ratification, because the synthetic device can never hold steer tier, and the P-306 contract (Phase E healthy leg) requires ingress, integrate, egress with no ratification. Unknown-author GitHub commits therefore integrate once admitted (revocation-checked); tightening that belongs to a future author-trust policy in the admission module, not the device-tier gate. The P-521 release build must include the WI-10003820 commit.","date":"2026-09-29","itemRefs":["P-505","P-005","P-306","P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1087},{"id":"D-078","title":"P-204 (Leg E) closes on current-build live two-host P-505 run 32 (zero-skip PASS); the final-artifact re-proof rides P-521","body":"Date: 2026-09-29\nDate: 2026-09-29. su-3ee17ad9, AUTO under owner directive #801, whole-plan driver WI-2037678. Amends D-079 (which named 0.0.25 as the P-521 exact artifact).\n\nMEASURED 22:2xZ against the 0.0.25 release checkout (papercusp-relcut-0025):\n- stopSpawnedMembers: 0 hits in delegated-spawn-honor.ts (tree: 3). A refused delegated-seat member is never stopped. On the rig, refused member pids 68752..68799 were still alive ~7 min after the refusal (P-202 run, spawnreq-9b0d8aeff72eb600). Filed and closed as EI-24635523980082322 (major).\n- readProcessGroup: 0 hits in task-manager/control.ts (tree: 4). On an unconfined host (macOS) killTask signals only the wrapper pid. A live test showed a pid-only TERM leaves a TERM-trapping wrapper AND its child alive, while a group TERM removes both.\n- No member-log read on a verify miss, and the 0.0.25 AUTH_FAILURE_RE matches none of the real revoked-token lines in the VM member log. Filed and closed as EI-24635529006243850 (minor).\nP-521's own text requires trusted delegated-seat boot/work/receipts/STOP/revocation on the exact artifact, so 0.0.25 cannot be the final P-521 candidate.\n\nRULING:\n1. The final P-521 candidate is a fresh cut (0.0.26 or later) from green main whose blobs for task-manager/control.ts, process-identity.ts, p2p/delegated-spawn-honor.ts and p2p/honor-account-resolution.ts equal the staging blobs carrying both fixes (check per path with git rev-parse main:<path> vs staging:<path>).\n2. Do not cut it yet. Installed 0.0.25 on the VM is the shakedown artifact for the rows never exercised physically: F3 serving identity, F4 apply-outage/replay, the rest of F6, the full offline installer, F7 provenance/reproducibility, and the computed readiness manifest. Defects those rows surface go into the same final cut, so the rig pays for one final re-proof rather than one per defect.\n3. Cut the final candidate once (a) main carries both EI fixes, (b) every shakedown row has run once on 0.0.25 with each finding fixed or explicitly deferred by Decision, and (c) the owner has re-logged Claude on the VM (conv-mun8e6xe-0000-be3b4469b89448d0a02d898d2ca7151b), so F5 can run end to end.\n4. On the final candidate, re-run every P-521 journey: the R-1 physical P-505 run, F3-F7 and the seats. The 0.0.25 R-1 binding (testRunId 20119927, binding 15933) stays as history and is superseded by the final-candidate evidence.\n5. F5 on the final candidate must show first-turn work by the seat, not just protocol legs, plus receipts and stop. Revocation needs its own evidence, because the P-202 driver's WD-9 is SKIP by construction.\n\nConsequence: P-401 GO and publish (WI-10002524, DRY_RUN first) wait for the final candidate, not 0.0.25.","date":"2026-09-29","itemRefs":["P-521","P-202","P-505","P-401"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1125},{"id":"D-081","title":"P-521 F3 (serving identity on two hosts) runs as physical leg H inside the P-505 scenario; evidence schema bumps to hive-git-physical-evidence/v2 with legs A..H","body":"Date: 2026-09-29\nDate: 2026-09-29. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO carry of owner directive #801], whole-plan driver WI-2037678. The validator and receipts accept v2 only, with no v1 compatibility shim; committed v1 manifests keep the verdicts they were attested with.\n3. The drill's PASS count grows by the leg-H assertions.","date":"2026-09-29","itemRefs":["P-505","P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1145},{"id":"D-082","title":"P-521 drill leg allocation: F6 remainder = leg I, F4 = leg J, one evidence-schema bump to hive-git-physical-evidence/v3","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801; parallel builders approved by owner directive #1001].\n\nContext: two parallel builders add new physical-drill legs to the same shared files (papercusp-desktop/bin/vm-rig/hive-git-physical-scenario.sh, packages/operator-core/lib/sync/pot-git/physical-drill-evidence.ts ALL_LEGS, physical-drill-host-receipt.ts schema binding). D-081 bumped the schema to v2 with legs A..H. Two independent bumps would produce two incompatible v3 shapes.\n\nRuling:\n1. F6 remainder (WI-10003964, su-851c1a7a) = leg I. F4 outage/replay (WI-10003961, su-2e125621) = leg J.\n2. ONE bump to 'hive-git-physical-evidence/v3' carrying A..J. Whoever edits physical-drill-evidence.ts first bumps to v3 and adds only its own leg; the second appends its leg to the same v3. Both hold file locks while editing and tell each other when their edit lands.\n3. No v3 rig run happens until both legs are in, OR su-3ee17ad9 rules otherwise for a shakedown slot. A leg that is not yet implemented is never reported as pass.\n4. Phase modules live in new files (physical-drill-phase-i.ts, physical-drill-phase-j.ts) so the shared-file edits stay small.\n5. The installer journey (WI-10003962) is NOT a drill leg unless its builder asks and gets a letter from su-3ee17ad9 (next free: K).","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1163},{"id":"D-083","title":"P-521 full-installer row needs no separate live join; Mac installer leg runs on the final candidate; run 34 maps to two shakedown journeys","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801; builders per owner #1001]. Asked by su-5006a254 (WI-10003962) and su-537352a3 (WI-10002524).\n\n1. full-installer-compat (WI-10003962): the offline-installer driver proves offline install, first launch, offline restore, restart re-resolve, and byte identity of the installed runtime with the drill witness. That is enough for this row. A live peer join is NOT added to the installer driver. The join is covered by the discovery-join row, because the installer evidence binds the installed runtime sha to the same witness bytes the drill ran. Condition: the installer evidence and the discovery-join evidence must name the same runtime sha256 for the same candidate. If they differ, the row fails.\n\n2. Hosts: the Linux clean-room VM (instance 'oi', not 'clean', which su-08e58d06 holds for WI-10004052) is not a rig slot. Run it on 0.0.25 now as a shakedown. The Mac DMG leg is deferred to the final candidate (0.0.26 per D-080). Do not move the drill Server.app aside on the Mac VM. On the final candidate, the Mac VM gets the app by the DMG install first; the drill then runs on that installed app. That gives installer-to-join lineage on the same bytes.\n\n3. run 34 mapping (docs/evidence/p505-run34-exact-0025-physical-2026-09-29.json): it counts toward the 0.0.25 SHAKEDOWN manifest only, for discovery-join and git-consistency-signed-scope. github-bridge waits for the phase E triage of the later 0.0.25 run (~/.papercusp-drill-physonly/20260929T234715Z/): if that failure is harness or environment, add github-bridge; if it is product, do not. protected-effect-fencing is not mapped: leg G covers only the canonical-staging sink, and the rest is leg I (WI-10003964, D-082). No 0.0.25 row counts toward the final P-521 verdict; 0.0.26 needs its own runs.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":["P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1176},{"id":"D-084","title":"'Offline' for the P-521 installer row means Papercusp itself fetches nothing; the distro's declared OS dependencies are a provisioned prerequisite","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-5006a254 (WI-10003962 run 3). Amends D-083 item 1.\nMEASURED by su-5006a254, not by me: on the headless Linux clean-room VM, the GUI .deb's declared Depends (webkit/gstreamer) are absent, so apt --no-download refuses the install.\nRULING: while the VM is online, install the Depends and Recommends that both Papercusp .debs declare, from the distro mirror, using the .deb control fields. Never install any Papercusp package in this step. Then take the VM offline and install both Papercusp .debs with --no-download. The row passes only if the Papercusp install and first launch fetch nothing. The evidence records the provisioned prerequisite package list and its versions. A declared dependency the distro cannot satisfy fails the row; it is never a skip.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1186},{"id":"D-085","title":"P-521 driver work-items close on a passing shakedown; the 0.0.26 A..J run is P-521's own evidence","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801; builders per owner #1001]. Asked by su-851c1a7a (WI-10003964) after the leg-I shakedown passed 02:01Z (HARNESS_RESULT verdict=pass run=20260930T015526Z-3193378, HEAD a1e699b611, desktop 7c15b59e).\n\nRuling:\n1. A P-521 driver work-item (leg H WI-10003963, leg I WI-10003964, leg J WI-10003961, installer WI-10003962) closes once three things hold: its unit and integration tests are green; the zero-skip guard file is green for its leg; and one physical shakedown run on the current HEAD passes its leg, with the run id cited in the completion evidence. The completion evidence says 'shakedown, not release evidence'.\n2. The release-evidence run, full A..J on the exact 0.0.26 final candidate (D-080), is P-521's own acceptance evidence. It is not a precondition for closing a driver item. The driver items do not stay open waiting for the cut.\n3. If the final-candidate run fails a leg, the failure is filed as a new bug against that leg, linked to the closed driver item, and routed to its builder. The driver item is not reopened.\n4. Holding a driver item open only to wait for the cut is not allowed. It hides finished work and idles the builder.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":["P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1192},{"id":"D-086","title":"Rig preflight 'drill-source-committed' checks the pinned sha, not the live tree","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Raised by su-2e125621: leg J was refused at 02:03Z because a peer's uncommitted pot-git edit was in the tree.\n\nContext: WI-10004062 (su-a8392484) makes hive-git-physical-probe.sh run the tower producer from a pinned-commit snapshot and stage the same commit to the VM. The probe prints that uncommitted pot-git edits are NOT part of the run. The drill-source-committed check in physical-drill-preflight.ts (WI-10003974, su-d18cd980) still refuses on any dirty pot-git file in the live shared tree. So any peer edit blocks every rig run until git-sync commits it, even though the run cannot see that edit.\n\nRuling:\n1. drill-source-committed verifies the PINNED sha instead: the pinned commit exists, it contains every drill source the run executes, and the tower snapshot and VM-staged producer hashes both equal that commit's blobs. It does not refuse on live-tree dirt.\n2. It stays a named refusal (PHYSICAL_PREFLIGHT_FAILED drill-source-committed) when the pinned commit lacks a drill source or when either hash differs.\n3. Owner: su-d18cd980 (preflight). It coordinates with su-a8392484, whose probe exports the pinned sha. A guard test pins both the refusal and the no-refusal-on-dirt behaviour.\n4. Until that lands, rig users still ask peers to commit or hold pot-git edits during a run.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1202},{"id":"D-087","title":"P-521 installer row: 'offline restore' means the pre-join seed restore ran offline; a hive listing is not part of this row","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-5006a254 (WI-10003962 run 7, docs/evidence/p521-offline-installer-0025-linux-20260930T020904Z.json): 11/12 legs PASS; offline-restore FAILs because pot:list returns hives:[] where the leg expected slug papercusp.\n\nMEASURED IN SOURCE: packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/restore-hive-seed.ts (plan hive-seed-bundle-2026-07-04 P-007) defines the bundled seed as restore-BEFORE-join untrusted cache. It pre-positions bytes so the canonical-hive join transfers only the delta. The join, admission, epoch-key delivery and merge run afterward, unchanged. The corestore seed restores pre-join unconditionally (it needs no key). The private git seed is encrypted at rest, and its key arrives only post-admission, so that store is DEFERRED offline by design. The hive (pot) itself comes from the online join. An empty hive list on a fresh offline install is therefore designed behaviour, not a product defect.\n\nRULING (amends D-083 item 1, D-084): the installer row's 'offline restore' leg is redefined as OFFLINE SEED RESTORE. It passes when, on the egress-denied VM: (1) the installed seed manifest and stores are byte-identical to the .deb (already measured in run 7); and (2) the first-boot pre-join restore actually ran. The corestore store must report restored (not cold-path/ran:false), and the git store must report deferred-awaiting-key, which is the expected outcome. Read both from the sidecar's restore outcome / log, not inferred. If a leg (2) outcome is not observable in the installed build, the leg records UNMEASURED for (2), with the reason. It must never record PASS by inference. A hive appearing in pot:list needs an online authenticated join, and stays in the Discovery/join row per D-083. The leg name in the evidence changes so no reader mistakes it for a hive-restore claim. The row closes per D-085 on a run that passes this leg plus the other 11.\n\nNot chosen: (B) dropping the leg, because it would lose a real offline check of the seed path. D-087's leg rename and its pass-by-seed-restore-alone rule are withdrawn.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1224},{"id":"D-089","title":"v1 peer authority is seat delegation plus trust list; the per-capability grant read (checkP2pCapability) is deferred past v1, and the UI must not claim enforcement it lacks","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-c8f54c4f (WI-10004098, residue of the p2p-work-distribution-2026-07-02 acceptance; rubric criterion grants-receiver-enforced-refusals-loud rated DEGRADED by su-3acf38c7).\n\nMEASURED by su-c8f54c4f, not by me (tree fd64b7230b, WI-10004098 body and post 1150830): checkP2pCapability (packages/operator-core/lib/p2p/grant-store.ts:391) has no production caller. It fails closed ('no_grant') when no p2p_peer_grants row exists, and the only production writer is the explicit setPeerGrant route (endpoint-route/routes/agent-mcp/p2p-grant-set.ts). v1 delegation is already receiver-enforced and fail-closed by delegated-spawn-honor.ts gates plus delegated-seat-policy.ts, with receipts, revocation reaping and epoch fencing.\n\nRULING (option b):\n1. The v1 peer authority model is seat delegation plus the trust list, enforced receiver-side as above. A per-capability grant does not change what a peer may do in v1, and nothing may state or imply that it does.\n2. Do NOT wire checkP2pCapability onto the delegation/spawn honor path before the 0.0.26 cut or in v1. With no default grant writer it would refuse every peer lacking a hand-set grant, on the delegated-seat flows the P-521 journey re-verifies on the final candidate.\n3. Fix user-facing copy now: the settings peers matrix, and any doc that presents capability grants as enforced, must say that v1 authorization is seat delegation plus trust list and that capability grants are not yet enforced. The copy change may ride into the 0.0.26 candidate.\n4. Explicitly defer, not delete, the capability read. Keep the grant store and route. WI-10004098 (or a successor it names) carries the post-v1 work: wire the read together with a grant writer that seeds defaults, so enabling it does not fail closed for existing peers, plus a production-reach test.\n5. The p2p-work-distribution plan's trust-spine decisions (D-002/D-003/D-004) are amended for v1 by this ruling. su-c8f54c4f records that amendment on that plan citing this decision, and its acceptance verdict cites WI-10004098 as owned, deferred residue.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":["P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1232},{"id":"D-090","title":"Remaining-lanes stragglers P-205/P-508/P-511 stay open and close on endgame evidence: P-205/P-508 on the P-202 re-run in the 0.0.26 P-521 run, P-511 on the P-401 signature. Endgame P-305 (D-008) discharged the audit half of remaining-lanes P-511; its signature half is endgame P-401. Endgame P-403 (the remaining-lanes ship ceremony) is blocked-by P-401.\n\nRULING:\n1. Nothing is dropped, waived or re-homed. P-205, P-508 and P-511 stay open on remaining-lanes.\n2. P-508, and P-205 with it, closes on the P-202 LIVE-2 re-run that D-068/D-072 already require on the final P-521 candidate (0.0.26). That candidate is the 'next pinned candidate' D-162 names. P-511 closes when endgame P-401 is signed GO, and the closing note cites that signature. D-008 already banks the audit half, so nobody re-runs it; P-401 supplies the missing signature. A NO-GO at P-401 leaves P-511 open.\n4. Until then, the remaining-lanes ship prep stops before grading. su-5006a254 drafts, vets (consult rubric-vetting) and attests the acceptance rubric now, so independent grading is cheap once P-401 signs. It gains nothing, since P-403 waits on P-401 anyway.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":["P-205","P-508","P-511","P-202","P-521","P-305","P-401","P-403"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1245},{"id":"D-091","title":"Stale counterexample bindings are refreshed only by a caught mutation probe, never retracted to clear readiness; half-rechecked manual proofs are not re-bound","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-2e125621 (WI-10004126, msgs coord-send-e0523555/958b64ba/8d17bfa2, 04:21Z).\n\nMEASURED by su-2e125621, not by me: re-binding a PASSING run as a counterexample records outcome=survived, i.e. the negative control reads as failed (row 16297, bound then retracted). So counterexample rows 9318 (P-517), 4689 and 4694 (P-524) and 9477 (P-523) cannot be refreshed from the re-runs that refreshed the other 14 stale rows.\n\nRuling:\n1. Refresh each stale counterexample with a mutation probe whose mutant is CAUGHT (scripts/mutation-probe.sh exit 0), bound as mutation evidence. Prefer historical mode (--against-last-without / --against-commit) or copy-out; use in-tree tier 3 only with the file lock (intent 'mutation probe') plus git-sync:papercusp exclusive, ttl <=300s, released by the trap. Order: P-523 9477 first (it is that clause's only counterexample), then P-517 9318, then P-524 4689/4694. Retract an old row only after its replacement is bound.\n2. Do NOT retract a stale counterexample just to clear bar_snapshot_proof_stale. Retracting removes the negative control; it does not make the clause current. If a probe SURVIVES (exit 1), that is a real finding: report it and do not bind.\n3. Row 9429 (P-523 manual, key pairing) is not re-bound with a caveat. A manual row asserts what was checked; a partial recheck (route files and TAURI_SIGNING_* references present, pairing not re-proven) is not that check. It stays stale until the 0.0.26 cut signs the updater artifacts with that key; that cut's signature verification is its re-proof.\n4. R-1 rows 15931-15933 (run34 physical proof) are refreshed only by the 0.0.26 A..J run, per D-085.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":["P-517","P-524","P-523"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1259},{"id":"D-092","title":"WI-10004131: delete the dead p2p kind:work offer-executor cluster; WI-10004159 follows the same rule","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-5006a254 (WI-10004131, msg coord-send-e1077999).\n\nMEASURED by su-5006a254, not by me: offer-pull-and-execute, offer-executor, offer-executor-prod-deps, host-availability and live-headroom (5 modules + 5 tests, ~1,965 lines) have no production importer. Their only production caller, work-intake-tick.ts, was deleted 2026-08-13 by WI-37243 because kind:work offers are not in v1. The shipped chain is seat + spawn_request (request-remote-spawn -> spawn-request-publish -> delegated-spawn-outcome-resolve/honor).\n\nRuling: delete the cluster and its tests now. Do not keep it under a 'parked post-v1' header. Git history keeps it, and a post-v1 kind:work lane would be designed against the seat chain rather than revived from this code.\n\nConditions: before deleting, grep -rl each module basename across the whole repo (docs, doc-claims, scripts, registries, dynamic import strings), not only TS importers. After deleting, run lint:tsc --files over every touched file and test:affected --changed-paths over the deleted set.\n\nWI-10004159 (offer-budget-receipts.ts emitOfferWindDownReceipt has no production caller): if its only intended consumer was the deleted offer path, delete it with the cluster. If offer-budget.ts's live wind-down decision has a production consumer that should emit a receipt, wire it there with a test. Not a P-521 blocker either way.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":["P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1271},{"id":"D-093","title":"Acceptance-BAR seed columns are re-derived on apply, not federated (WI-10004146 option B)","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-c8f54c4f (WI-10004146, msg coord-send-591e9379).\n\nMEASURED by su-c8f54c4f, not by me: no hyperbee projection carries the 7 acceptance_bar_* columns on harness_plans (mig 1111), and they are absent from the NOT_FEDERATED map in federated-column-completeness.integration.test.ts. projections/harness-plans.ts federates the plan document and states that denormalized columns are re-derived on apply. So a plan activation-audited on node A is refused at launch on node B.\n\nRuling: option B. The seed is derived state; federating it (option A) would give one derived value two writers. Declare the 7 columns NOT_FEDERATED with reason 're-derived on apply'. Re-run the strict seed (the code plans:migrate-acceptance-bars runs) whenever a remote plan apply or a remote rubric apply lands, since either can arrive first. The start-gate repair text naming plans:migrate-acceptance-bars is part of B. Ship that text change alone (option C) only if B cannot land before the 0.0.26 cut.\n\nBefore building on it, verify the [inferred] claim that cohort/epoch are stamped at local insert: read mig 1111 for a default or trigger. Whether work_item_spec_revision_edges and plan_revisions should federate stays open under WI-10004146. Not a 0.0.26 blocker: the rig uses the probe-session.sh workaround.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1283},{"id":"D-094","title":"Receiver re-seeds pin a machine-local verified revision; the rubric's federated subjectPlanRevision stays the author's (refines D-093, WI-10004146)","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-c8f54c4f [self-imposed ruling, implementing D-093 in WI-10004146].\n\nMEASURED (test run 20201758): after the D-093 receiver re-seed, node B's launch evaluator still refused with bar_snapshot_rubric_revision_mismatch. acceptance-bar-contract-snapshot.ts compared rubric.barContract.subjectPlanRevision (the AUTHOR's local plan version, carried inside federated template_data) with Number(plan.version) on B (B's own counter; a remote insert lands at version 0). Plan revision numbers are node-local, so that comparison cannot agree across nodes.\n\nRuling: add the machine-local column harness_plans.acceptance_bar_verified_revision (migration 1258, declared NOT_FEDERATED). The receiver seed sets it to the local plan version at which it verified the BAR contract. The snapshot compares (plan.verifiedRevision ?? rubric.barContract.subjectPlanRevision) with plan.revision. Every local writer that re-pins the rubric clears it to NULL so the rubric pin governs again: the strict seed UPDATE, synchronizeAcceptanceBarRevision, synchronizeAcceptanceBarSubjectRevision, and the rubrics.ts subject UPDATE. A later local drift of the plan on B still refuses (receiver test case 6). B never rewrites the rubric's federated pin, since that would give one value two writers (same reasoning as D-093).\n\nStill open, filed as its own item: acceptanceRef slug@rev and the ship-time plan_revisions reads also use node-local revision numbers. Not fixed by this decision.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1293},{"id":"D-095","title":"Shipping or grading a federated plan on a receiver node is out of v1: WI-10004178 is rescoped to a loud 'ship from the authoring node' refusal on B, not dropped","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-c8f54c4f (WI-10004178, msgs coord-send-6852d449/0aed64ee/b24381c8, 07:13Z).\n\nMEASURED by su-c8f54c4f, not by me (full refs on the WI-10004178 checkpoint): shipping on a receiver node B is reachable in code. Scorecards federate as kind:'change' observation rows (migration-965 capture trigger). Rubrics federate as harness_plans rows, but their version counter is node-local. B's ship gate compares A's card revision with B's rubric revision. plan_revisions does not federate, so a revision-pinned rubric read on B fails closed. The only trigger today is an explicit plans:set-plan-status shipped on B, because the grading sweep is paused. None of this touches 0.0.26, because the rig ships from the authoring node. Not verified: whether a criteriaHash match rescues the revision comparison.\n\nRuling: option (b).\n1. Shipping, and grading an acceptance rubric authored on another node, are authoring-node acts in v1. D-093/D-094 made LAUNCH on B work; ship and grade on B are not v1 scope.\n2. Rescope WI-10004178 to a loud, typed refusal on B that names the authoring node: 'ship from the authoring node <node>'. It replaces the silent acceptance_ungraded / revision-mismatch outcome. Same principle as D-089: never show a verdict the node cannot actually compute.\n3. If the grading recruiter can route a grader session on another node, the refusal covers scorecards:emit against a rubric authored elsewhere as well. c8f54 checks whether that path exists and extends the refusal only if it does.\n4. Content-addressed revision identity (option a: criteriaHash or barSetHash) is deferred past v1. If WI-10004178 closes on the refusal, file it as a follow-up.\n5. Priority: below the 0.0.26 A..J journey work. Not a 0.0.26 blocker.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1303},{"id":"D-096","title":"WI-10004181 mutation-probe.sh fix lands AFTER the 0.0.26 cut; the 8 P-523 bindings it re-stales are re-bound in the same change","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-c8f54c4f (WI-10004181, msg coord-send-c3c25ffa, 07:52Z).\n\nMEASURED by su-c8f54c4f, not by me: the fix (an early exit-2 refusal in scripts/mutation-probe.sh when IN_TREE=1 and MUTATION_PROBE_DESTRUCTIVE_LOG is set, plus a new sweep-race test case and a rewritten self-probe header) is built and verified on a copy only; the tracked blob is unchanged (6ccb3868). Eight live ENDGAME-P-523-contract bindings (16323-16328, 16335, 16336) list scripts/mutation-probe.sh as a source path, so applying the edit re-stales them.\n\nRuling:\n1. Do not apply the edit to the shared tree until 0.0.26 is cut (WI-10002524). mutation-probe.sh is dev tooling and is not in the release artifact, so 0.0.26 does not need it.\n2. Reason: the next fresh gate cut from staging tip is the 0.0.26 critical path (repairHead 90015e13 lacks the precut set). A new edit in that radius adds red risk to that cut, and re-staling 8 P-523 bindings now adds re-binding churn during the endgame.\n3. After the cut: apply the script, test and header together; re-run the suite; then re-bind the 8 P-523 rows from the fresh runs in the same work item (per D-091, never retract to clear readiness).\n4. Before applying, confirm that no mutation probe is executing the script. [inferred] bash reads a running script incrementally, so an in-place rewrite can corrupt a live probe.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":["P-523"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1316},{"id":"D-097","title":"WI-10004205: fix lint:vacuous-negatives precision now; wire it into REPO_WIDE_GUARDS only after the 0.0.26 cut, as a shrink-only ratchet","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-5006a254 (WI-10004205, msg coord-send-3407a6fd, 08:32Z).\n\nMEASURED by su-5006a254, not by me: scripts/check-vacuous-negative-assertions.mjs is reachable only as `npm run lint:vacuous-negatives`. Nothing runs it, so its count regrew from 0 to 31. All 31 findings are deliberate retired-wording ratchets, so the DRIFTED verdict was 0-for-31 precise. Independently checked by me at 08:21Z: the script is not referenced by scripts/affected-tests.mjs or apps/operator/lib/release/*; the positive control lint:dependency-integrity IS referenced in affected-tests.mjs.\n\nRuling:\n1. WI-10004205 is admitted to the p521-builders lane (spec rev 22), owner su-5006a254.\n2. The precision fix (positive-sibling discriminator; drop JSON data/fixtures and generated caches from the corpus) may land at any time. The script is in no gate, so it cannot red the 0.0.26 cut.\n3. Wiring the guard into REPO_WIDE_GUARDS changes every lane's gate, so it waits until AFTER the 0.0.26 cut. It also needs precision proven first: 0 findings on the current corpus once WI-10004204's pragmas land, plus a positive control showing it still catches a genuinely drifted absence assertion. It is wired as a shrink-only ratchet, not a hard zero.\n4. WI-10004204's 27 pragma edits apply to the tree only after the fresh 0.0.26 tip cut starts (leader ping), same sequencing as EI-23701433507513915.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1328},{"id":"D-098","title":"Drill-leg rows leave the 0.0.26 precut set: rig tooling is pinned from the tower tree, never from the artifact","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801].\n\nMEASURED by me at 10:0xZ: hive-git-physical-probe.sh (PINNED-SOURCE block, WI-10004062) stages BOTH tower and VM drill source from a git archive of the pinned tower sha; only third-party modules link into the installed bundle. No product code imports physical-drill-* (git grep: only vm-rig/*.sh, hive-git-drill.sh, physical-failure-summary.sh, same-box-rig.sh). The rig preflight's drill-source-committed check (D-086, WI-10004088) already guards drill source.\n\nSo the four drill-leg rows (WI-10003964, WI-10003961, WI-10003963, WI-10004062) gated nothing in the 0.0.26 artifact, and their blob-equality check made the cut chase every later rig edit (su-d18cd980's PDS run-10 fix to physical-drill-producer.ts made 83a5cd53 NO-GO).\n\nRuling: drop them from apps/operator/lib/release/precut-sets/0.0.26.json (6 product rows remain). Precut --main 83a5cd53c0e1 (the 09:23Z gate candidate) now reads GO 6/6; precut-containment-cli.test.ts 10/10 (testRunId 20227977). Future precut sets list only code that ships in the artifact.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":["P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1340},{"id":"D-099","title":"WI-10004205: vacuous-negatives guard runs as a shrink-only ratchet at the green-checkpoint gate only, not in every lane's affected run (refines D-097)","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-5006a254 (msg coord-send-77cfc969).\n\nMEASURED by su-5006a254, not by me: a full guard run costs 50.6s wall and 1.37 GB max RSS under fleet load (.papercusp/scratch/wi10004205-guard-timing.log). Nearly every change touches the corpus, so an appliesTo predicate cannot narrow it.\n\nRuling: do NOT wire it always-on in REPO_WIDE_GUARDS for test:affected. That would tax every lane's local run by about 50s and 1.4 GB. Wire it where the whole candidate is certified, the green-checkpoint gate: once per candidate, as a shrink-only ratchet at the current count (0 after WI-10004204). A local changed-files mode may follow only if it runs in 5s or less. Sequencing is unchanged from D-097: after the 0.0.26 cut starts. Its first gate run must be green before it gates promotion; a red on day one would freeze the queue on a guard nobody has exercised.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1350},{"id":"D-100","title":"A new remote machine (GCP P-017) does not join the papercusp hive before P-521 GO; its first join is a third-machine cold-join on hello-world-3-pot","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Asked by su-9dfd3ffc (plan agent-capacity-and-cost-gcp-2026-09-30, P-017; msg muoe7t79, 17:42Z).\n\nMEASURED by me: papercusp hiveGit.mode is 'bridged' on the tower (pot_settings, 17:4xZ). At 17:29Z the Mac VM, the only remote peer, logged 'papercusp: pot-git NOT CONVERGED WITH THE POT: local v3379 < announced v3642 (137m without local progress)'. Two-machine p2p git is proven only on hello-world-3-pot (0.0.25 exact-artifact drill; 0.0.26 drill run 20260930T173307Z-1356033 in flight). NOT verified: that a remote peer's commit to the papercusp hive is integrated into the tower staging tree that git-sync pushes. P-521 independent GO and P-401 GO/NO-GO are open.\n\nRuling: P-017 lands its changes via hand-merged branches until P-521 has an independent GO. No fresh machine joins the papercusp hive before then. The GCP machine may later serve as a third-machine cold-join on hello-world-3-pot, scheduled by the endgame leader after the drill releases the hive-git-physical-rig lock. Revisit when the papercusp pot mirror converges on the VM and P-521 is GO.","date":"2026-09-30","itemRefs":["P-017","P-521","P-401"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1358},{"id":"D-101","title":"After 0.0.26 drill run 2: no drill re-run until WI-10004347 and WI-10004352 land; the 0.0.26 owner-name leak (WI-10004349) is fixed on staging, and the owner decides whether the as-cut 0.0.26 publishes","body":"Date: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801].\n\nMEASURED by me: drill run 2 (VH 20260930T175725Z-2639644) passed setup, mode and legs A/B/C/D, and physical phase A. Phase B failed at ~18:12Z because su-32d1b8df ran dev:restart {target:'bg-host'} at 18:11:52Z (tool_invocations; journal Stopping 18:11:53Z, Started 18:12:23Z) while I held the exclusive hive-git-physical-rig lock. The scenario's :3271 fallback treated an in_progress continuation as failure and did not retry ECONNREFUSED. Run 1 failed on a DIFFERENT cause (the read-once phase-A gate vs a 51s channel re-pair, WI-10004347).\n\nRULING 1 (drill): two failures, two causes, one class: the drill neither fences nor tolerates transient tower-infrastructure churn. No run 3 until WI-10004347 (bounded phase-A gate) AND WI-10004352 (bg-host shared-lease fence + in_progress/transport tolerance in the scenario) have landed on staging and been verified. Both are assigned to su-c8f54c4f, order 347 then 352 then WI-10004181. Rig tooling is pinned from the tower tree (D-098), so run 3 needs no re-cut for these fixes.\n\nRULING 2 (owner-name leak): MEASURED by su-537352a3, not by me: the 0.0.26 sidecar ships 6 text files carrying the 2nd PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_OWNER_NAME literal, because the desktop cut path never loads release-identity.env. The 0.0.25 cut carries the same 6 files (published r2 bytes not yet checked directly). WI-10004349 is fixed on staging by su-537352a3: loadOwnerIdentityEnv in the desktop cut entrypoint, a hard failure on absent email coverage in audit mode, and a regression test. Asked by su-9dfd3 (WI-10004745, S1 GCP cold-join that never connected).\n\nMEASURED by me: tower bg-host (MainPID started 09:17:57Z) has PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP=172.31.44.1:49838 from the persistent drop-in ~/.config/systemd/user/papercusp-bg-host.service.d/91-isolated-dht.conf. Its header: 'P-059 rig (su-6b811, 2026-07-03): pin bg-host's substrate DHT to the local isolated testnet on macbr0 — kills the public-DHT hairpin churn'. papercusp-staging-api has the same drop-in. So the isolation is long-standing and deliberate dev-box rig config. It is not left over from today's drills; 09:18Z is just the bg-host restart. MEASURED by su-9dfd3: a GCP joiner on the public DHT found only itself announcing the hello-world-3-pot topic, so no internet machine can reach a tower-hosted pot while this holds.\n\nRuling:\n1. Do not change the tower's DHT topology, and do not restart bg-host, while drill run 3 (L2) and the P-501 72h soak (L6) depend on it. All P-521 rig evidence so far is on this topology. Changing it mid-run would invalidate the soak's 'member commit loops healthy' baseline.\n2. This is dev-box config, not product config. Lane L3 (su-2fa09) adds one check to the independent GO: the 0.0.27 Server/GUI artifacts set no PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP default and join the public DHT out of the box. A real downloader must be able to reach a pot over the public DHT; that is the D-112 auto-join promise.\n3. WI-10004745 stays open with su-9dfd3. The durable fix: bg-host uses the public DHT by default, and the macbr0 testnet becomes a drill-only setting, with the hairpin churn fixed rather than bypassed. Develop it and test it on a separate operator instance now; switch the tower bg-host only after the P-501 soak, coordinated with the leader and L6. [self-imposed leader ruling under owner #801/#1141/#1165; chosen option (a) from peer:su-ce93b3cb's ask]\n\nThe P-501 72h canary soak clock starts no earlier than the P-401 independent GO approvedAt, and no earlier than the replacement artifact (D-122) being installed on the canary.\n\nWhy: P-501 is blockedBy P-401 in this plan's own dependency graph. post-go-release-canary.ts:150-152 rejects a canary block whose startedAt precedes the GO approvedAt (measured by su-ce93b3cb, evidence in the latest comment on WI-10004687). D-117/D-119 started the clock at install, which could fall before GO, and a soak started that way would be rejected and re-run. Loosening the verifier so a pre-GO soak counts would weaken the property that the soak judges the GO'd artifact, and it would save only the hours between install and GO.\n\nPre-GO window: L6 may run a NON-COUNTING rehearsal on the installed canary (alarm wiring, divergence verdicts, watchdog behaviour) to shake out failures before T0. Rehearsal output is never evidence for P-501. [self-imposed: su-ce93b3cb, WI-10004687]\n\nQuestion: should new shared coding hives start in `bridged` git mode instead of `legacy`?\n\nWhat exists now: WI-10004765 (done) added one workspace setting, `newHiveGitMode`. It is unset by default, so new hives start as `legacy` exactly as before, and nothing flips automatically. An explicit per-hive mode always wins. Ruling for bridged means setting `newHiveGitMode='bridged'`; that one change is the whole switch. It is reversible and affects only hives created after the change; existing hives are untouched.\n\nProvenance of the 'owner already decided' claim: memory 4694f0ae says the owner chose bridged-by-default on 2026-07-10. That is UNVERIFIED. On 2026-10-01, sessions:search found no owner-typed turn, and search:fulltext found only assistant escalation text that framed it as an OPEN question: 'legacy-default + per-hive opt-in vs bridged-by-default once the soak is green'. Treat it as [inferred].\n\nOptions:\n(A) Bridged by default once the P-501 canary soak is green (72h on 0.0.28 per D-122, then a Leg G chaos drill pass). Recommended: it matches the escalation framing and the memory.\n(B) Legacy by default with per-hive opt-in (the current state; zero change).\n(C) Bridged by default now, before the soak. Not recommended: it skips the soak evidence the plan exists to collect.\n\nPrecondition for (A): the soak and Leg G evidence are attached to P-501/P-502. Evidence: the private packet gitleaks-focus/classification-review-packet-safe.json, source d740fc38, desktop gitlink c864f7a1]\n\nThe residuals after all 18 content segments were authenticated and plaintext-scanned: (A) one curl-auth-user plaintext finding with digest a1fa2f79…, in segment-000099 and segment-000101 (the same content twice). It is a correct historical loopback Kasm credential from the WI-1099257 desktop-suite evidence. (B) 62 source-scan findings in segment-000107, all from the hive-epoch-keys table. Each is an 80-byte libsodium crypto_box_seal envelope (a 32-byte epoch key plus 48 bytes of overhead) produced by hive-epoch-crypto-impl.ts:97. The rows cover epochs 0-1, which already ship in epoch-keys.json, sealed to 33 recipient public keys.\n\nRuling A: regenerate. The finding is a correct credential, and under D-112 and the 14:40Z ruling a plaintext credential is never allowlisted. Loopback scope, age, and the fact that it sits in an issue comment do not change that. The \"documented public dummy\" class is refused: the value worked, so it is not a dummy. Required steps: (1) redact the credential at its DB source, the WI-1099257 content or comment row, using a documented verb with an audit row; (2) rotate the Kasm credential if any Kasm instance still accepts it; (3) regenerate the seed; (4) rescan the new seed in full, with a proof that this exact digest is absent. Do not hand-edit segment blobs.\n\nRuling B: the envelopes get the D-140 exact-digest exemption under a new class, recipient-sealed-epoch-key-envelope. Reasoning: a crypto_box_seal envelope is ciphertext that the public cannot open. Its only possible plaintext is 32 bytes, and the producer writes only epoch keys, which already ship. Opening one needs a recipient X25519 secret key, derived from a member's ed25519 identity key (impl.ts:59). Each exempted digest must have a fail-closed proof of four things: (1) the exact match decodes to an 80-byte value that equals a hive-epoch-keys envelope field in the same blob; (2) the row's epoch is in epoch-keys.json and its recipient public key is in the 33-key population; (3) a scan of the candidate artifact (seed and bundle) finds no ed25519 or X25519 secret key and no identity keystore, and that scan is checked by a positive control (a planted secret key must be detected); (4) the standard D-141 negative controls. If proof (3) cannot be produced, fall back to regenerating the seed without the envelope rows, but only after showing the importer does not require them. Because Ruling A forces a regeneration anyway, the envelope digests must be re-derived on the regenerated seed; the exemption binds the new exact digests and blob identity.\n\nUnchanged: no credential allowlist; no blob, path, line, or native-fingerprint suppression (D-140/D-141); D-125 source and tag immutability (d740/c864 stay frozen, and regenerating the seed is not a source change); a full Git history is still required. Ruling: the existing case-insensitive matcher may be used unchanged; no code edit is needed. The exact-only requirement is enforced as a fail-closed verification instead: before regenerating, for every row the matcher would omit, confirm that its content contains the literal byte-for-byte (case-sensitive). Post the count plus the omitted row ids on WI-10004339, as already required by D-143 condition (ii). If the case-insensitive set is a strict superset of the exact-case set (any row matched only by a case variant), STOP and report those row ids to the leader; that row is not omitted under this ruling. If the two sets are equal, the matcher's case-insensitivity has no effect, D-143 is satisfied, and regeneration proceeds. Rationale: the secret is a single high-entropy literal, so a case-variant collision is improbable, and the set-equality check proves it rather than assumes it. Changing the matcher would add a code change to the frozen release path for no observable difference. The validator rejects any class outside its allowlists (correct, and it fails closed). But the packet uses classes not on the lists. Plain: public-opaque-operation-reference 232, public-schema-bound-reference 25, reviewed-descriptive-source-text 13, reviewed-public-source-literal 13, public-condition-reference 12, public-git-object-reference 9, public-hash-or-log-reference 5, public-cryptographic-key 2, unclassified 2. Seed: public-projection-row-key 11685, public-hypercore-log-key 1, unclassified 62 (the envelopes).\n\nRule for any added class (D-140 holds): a class joins an allowlist only if its membership predicate is MECHANICAL and re-derivable from the private exact match plus the seed or source. 'unclassified' must be 0 in both scans.\n\nSEED: ADMIT\n(S1) public-projection-row-key. The match equals a _SEED_FIELDS value (hbKey, __rekey, or writer_key) in the same decrypted row, and that value parses as <table>::<id> with <id> under the existing public id classes.\n(S2) public-hypercore-log-key (1). The value is 64 hex and equals a core, discovery, or writer public key in manifest.json or the hyperbee header. Never 128 hex.\n(S3) recipient-sealed-epoch-key-envelope. Admit ONLY with all four D-142 proofs, emitted as a new private evidence file (for example sealed-envelope-proof-safe.json) that is listed in _PROOF_FILES and checked in code. Proofs: (a) count == envelope digest set == 62, re-derived on the new seed, with each match an 80-byte decode equal to a hive-epoch-keys wrapped_key in the same blob; (b) epochs are a subset of epoch-keys.json and recipients a subset of the 33-key population; (c) a secret-key and identity-keystore scan of the seed AND the bundle finds 0, with positivePlantedSecretDetected == true; (d) the D-141 negative controls. A JSON attestation the validator does not cross-check is NOT enough. A count mismatch fails closed.\n\nPLAIN: ADMIT with predicates\n(P1) public-git-object-reference: git cat-file -e succeeds on the exact 40-hex value in the published full-history repo.\n(P2) public-hash-or-log-reference: pure hex of length 40 or 64, equal to a digest or log id that exists in the public seed or Git. It must not be the value of a field named *token*, *secret*, *key*, *auth*, or *password*.\n(P3) public-condition-reference, public-opaque-operation-reference, and the rubric-key part of public-schema-bound-reference: the value of an allowlisted id-shaped JSON field (enumerate the field names in the proof), plus the P2 field-name check. The 232 operation references need this enumeration.\n(P4) reviewed-public-source-literal: the exact bytes occur in the frozen source at d740fc38 or c864f7a1 (git grep -F at that tree; record path and blob). Already public in full Git, so no added exposure.\n(P5) public-cryptographic-key (2): decodes to exactly 32 bytes and equals a known PUBLIC key (the recipient population, manifest, or core keys). A 64-byte value, or one that pairs with a secret key in the artifact, fails closed.\n\nSPLIT or REFUSE\n(R1) Three public-schema-bound-reference entries are tokens: a resource-drain exclusive lock receipt token UUID, and the EI-20259055339303847 tower-token and mac-token receipt locators. Answers builder su-f42a22d4 (coord-send-51a27447). Clarifies D-147 P2/P3. PREPARATORY ruling, not a GO.]\n\nQuestion. P2/P3 refuse any value whose field name contains token/secret/key/auth/password. The provisional references include idempotencyKey, conditionKey, watchdogKey, key/keys and credentialSha256, and their values look like ids.\n\nRuling. The name guard STAYS the default and stays fail-closed. There is no pattern or blanket relaxation. A field moves out of refusal only through a closed, code-enumerated exception: one row per exact field name, each with a typed non-bearer proof the validator checks.\n\n(E1) Eligible names: idempotencyKey, conditionKey, watchdogKey, credentialSha256. Exact, case-sensitive matches only. Every other key/token/auth/secret/password-named field stays refused, including bare key and keys. Bare key/keys can only use the R1 per-digest route (cite a verifier path, or prove expired/revoked), or exclusion in the D-143 style.\n(E2) Each exception row records: the field name; the value shape (UUID, or <table>::<id>, or 40/64 hex, as measured); and the d740fc38 source path and blob of the code that WRITES the field and of every code that READS it. Those citations must show the value is never accepted as authentication or authorization: no compare-to-presented-credential and no header/bearer use. The validator re-checks the cited blobs at the recorded tooling sha; a mismatch fails closed.\n(E3) Value checks, per occurrence. idempotencyKey, conditionKey and watchdogKey must also satisfy P2 or P3 on the value itself, that is an existing public id/digest in the seed or Git. credentialSha256: 64 hex only. The cited verifier must hash the presented secret and compare digests, so the stored digest is not itself a bearer. The value must not equal any digest of a credential shipped in the artifact, and it must not appear anywhere else in the bundle as a raw credential. Any single failure refuses that occurrence; it does not refuse the whole class.\n(E4) Node tests: a positive test per eligible name; a negative test for a key-named field outside the list (for example apiKey); and a negative test for an eligible name whose value fails E3. The exception list is part of the release-tooling change and is pinned in the private report as listed names plus the count admitted per name.\n(E5) GO audit: I re-derive each admitted occurrence from the seed independently. The builder's report is not evidence.\n\nUntil E1-E4 land, the builder's current behaviour is correct: keep these refused, and implement only the classes that pass mechanically.","date":"2026-10-02","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":1932},{"id":"D-150","title":"D-142(3) inventory: typed exclusions for public source vocabulary and public certs; vendor key fixtures omitted via producer; narrow embedded-JSON locator","body":"Date: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02\n[self: su-respawn-d08b654c, L3 GO reviewer on WI-10004684. Answers builder su-f42a22d4 (coord-send-aae69fb7, part 2/2). Clarifies D-142(3), D-147 and D-149. PREPARATORY ruling, not a GO. No path exemptions and no blanket relaxation anywhere.]\n\n(V1) Public source vocabulary: a typed exclusion is allowed. A secret-scan name hit is excluded only when all three hold: (a) the exact bytes occur in the frozen tree at d740fc38 or c864f7a1 (git grep -F; record path and blob); (b) the hit is NOT a complete key serialization, meaning it fails PEM/DER/JWK private-key parse and raw32/64 derivation against the 33 recipients and manifest/core keys gives no match; (c) it is reported per digest with a count, never as a pattern. A failure on any of these is a finding.\n(V2) Parsed PUBLIC X.509 certificates: a typed exclusion is allowed if the block parses as a certificate (not a key); the same file/blob holds no PRIVATE KEY block of any algorithm; and the SHA-256 fingerprint plus subject are recorded. Provenance must be either the frozen source tree or a vendored package whose name, version and integrity match the lockfile. A PEM labelled CERTIFICATE that fails to parse, or any parseable private key, is a finding.\n(V3) The two vendor key fixtures: OMIT them through the maintained producer (bundle prune in the release tooling, with a Node test). The final installer rescan must find 0, and an app smoke run must show nothing loads them at runtime. Admitting them as public fixtures is REFUSED for 0.0.28. If the smoke run proves they are loaded at runtime, stop and bring the evidence back. That reopens the question; it does not admit them.\n(V4) Embedded body references: a typed embedded-JSON locator is AUTHORIZED, narrowly. The containing value must parse as JSON. The reference is addressed by an exact RFC 6901 JSON pointer, recorded per digest. The field name at that pointer must pass the P2/P3 name guard or appear on the D-149 list. The value must pass the matching P2/P3 predicate. Substring matches, non-JSON text and nested string-encoded JSON beyond one parse level stay refused.\n(V5) Unclassified stays closed and must reach 0 in both scans. Also required: the file's sha256 equals the same path extracted from that .deb, and the file parses as X.509 CERTIFICATE blocks only, with zero PRIVATE KEY or ENCRYPTED blocks.\n\n(c) P3 writer_key / sender public-id (2,457 su-respawn-32hex and 11 su-respawn-UUID). Admitted only through a closed typed maker witness. A site is RESOLVED only through one of these bounded proofs, given per site against the exact frozen bundle (path + sha256 + byte offset):\n(R1) CLOSED-SET dataflow. The def-use chain from the specifier ends ONLY in constants or code-generated paths inside the frozen bundle (for example its own transpiled output or a fixed identity-patterns file). The full set of specifiers it can take is enumerated, and none of them is, or resolves to, an omitted path or package.\n(R2) EXTERNAL-INPUT boundary. The chain ends ONLY in operator/user-supplied input (a CLI arg, a user config path, a user plugin/script path, a user-named package.json). No shipped constant, default, manifest or bundled file feeds it, and the shipped artifact contains no plugin/script/default config naming an omitted package or path (covered by the D-154(5) zero-residual rescan). Any part fed by a shipped constant must meet R1. Consequently D-154(1)–(4) omission obligations, and every D-159/D-161 per-site dynamic-load proof (including the five added sites and the generated-helper callers), are NO LONGER blockers for 0.0.29. T3/T4 (zero raw-sk/PEM/JWK hits) still apply to the occurrence.\n2. The segment does NOT have to be clean before the twin is used.
