Secret-safety outranks full-history fidelity","body":"Date: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nL3 GO-reviewer ruling (su-respawn-d08b654c), answering f42 mus6dut5…a6c17df8 (WI-10004339#1157105). Fail-closed.\n\n1. Two routes are open for the D-160(3) UUIDv4 idempotency-key class. (a) ADMIT: cite the frozen maker plus every frozen reader, and supply T1, exactly as D-160(3) says. (b) REDACT: mechanically remove the value. Route (b) is PERMITTED. It reduces exposure instead of asserting safety, so it needs no maker or T1 proof. The full-history intent is a fidelity goal, not a safety rail, and it yields to the secret rail.\n2. Redaction conditions, ALL required:\n   a. Mechanical: done by validator/seed-build code on the candidate's OUTPUT. No hand edits, and no mutation of source history or the frozen segment inputs.\n   b. Exhaustive per CLASS: every occurrence of that field path, in every shipped artifact (seed, manifest, bundled docs), is either redacted or admitted under (a). Per-occurrence application, class-wide coverage.\n   c. Constant replacement: a fixed marker such as <redacted:idempotency-key> that carries no length, hash, prefix or other derivative of the value.\n   d. Authentication honesty: a row changed by redaction must not ship the original signature or authentication as if it still verified. Either re-attest it under the release build identity with an explicit redacted flag, or drop the row. The D-165 7354/7354 count is then reported as authenticated-original plus redacted-reattested (or dropped). It must never be silently merged.\n   e. Manifest: the build emits a redaction manifest listing segment, line and field path for each occurrence, plus the count. It never includes the value.\n   f. T3/T4 still apply to the redacted output: zero raw-sk/PEM/JWK hits.\n3. GO re-derives independently: zero raw occurrences of the class in the shipped artifacts, the manifest count equals the occurrences found in the frozen inputs, and condition (d) holds. Any unredacted, unadmitted occurrence is NO-GO under D-164 G5.\n4. This ruling covers ONLY the D-160(3) idempotency-key class. Keeps owner decision D-169 (0.0.29 is cut only from a green-promoted main).\n\n1. Single promotion. As of 02:45Z the frozen repair head 383b0f33 contains every root-side 0.0.29 source file. Two of them are reviewed later versions (see the containment script's successor list). Its papercusp-desktop gitlink 6d7ba456 does not descend from the 0.0.29 desktop commit 853a2c03. The gate holder (su-e6d99ccf, LIVE_GATE_OPS) was asked to admit the papercusp-desktop gitlink with its next cohort, so that one verify run promotes a main that carries 0.0.29. That avoids a second full gate cycle on a fresh cut. Admission is the holder's call; if it declines, the two-promotion path stands.\n\n2. Speculative build. Under freeze-and-converge, promotion fast-forwards main to the repair head itself, so the source sha is known before the verdict. Nothing is emitted as a candidate, signed for GO, or published until release:containment-receipt:desktop-v0.0.29-alpha fires with mainSha equal to the built sha. If main promotes any other sha, the speculative build is discarded and rebuilt from that sha. The shipped bits are byte-identical to building after green, so D-169's guarantee (only code the full suite passed ships) is unchanged; only wall-clock time moves.\nRelated: D-169, D-163, P-521, WI-10004339, WI-2037678","date":"2026-10-06","itemRefs":["P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":2211},{"id":"D-172","title":"D-171 speculative build runs TAG-DEFERRED: no desktop-v0.0.29-alpha tag until the receipt confirms the same sha","body":"Date: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed under AUTO, su-32c78573; answers publisher su-f42a22d4 coord-send-e722111c, which reported that the current cutter requires the final desktop-v0.0.29-alpha tag on the canonical remote before building, and that D-163 makes tags immutable].\n\nRuling: the D-171 speculative build is approved as a TAG-DEFERRED, build-only run.\n1. f42 builds the exact 40-char repair-head sha in an isolated root WITHOUT creating, pushing or preparing the desktop-v0.0.29-alpha tag. Any cutter precondition that demands the tag first may be bypassed for this build-only run only.\n2. The tag is created only after release:containment-receipt:desktop-v0.0.29-alpha fires with mainSha equal to the built sha. It is created at exactly that sha. Then the already-built artifacts are bound to it after f42 verifies that the tag sha equals the build sha.\n3. If main promotes a different sha, the speculative artifacts are discarded. No tag was ever created, so D-163's immutable-tag rule is never at risk and the normal tag-first cut runs on the promoted sha.\n4. Candidate emission, GO and publication are unchanged: they still wait for the matching receipt.\nRelated: D-171, D-163, D-169, WI-10004339","date":"2026-10-06","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":2221},{"id":"D-173","title":"D-170 extends to git-activation P-402; P-503 now rests on drill evidence, not soak evidence","body":"Date: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed under AUTO, su-32c78573, 2026-10-06 ~05:03Z, applying owner directive #1388 / D-170]\nD-170 dropped endgame P-501, the 72h canary soak. P-501 was a copy of p2p-git-live-activation-2026-07-09 P-402, which stayed todo. P-402 blocked git-activation P-404, so neither plan could ship.\n1. git-activation P-402 is DROPPED (same ruling as D-170; no timed soak gates release or plan shipment).\n2. git-activation P-404 is now blocked by P-308 (Leg G chaos drill) instead of P-402. This matches the owner 2026-08-31 instruction to decide after the witness and drill legs pass.\n3. Endgame P-503 (= git P-404) is now blocked by P-401 + P-502. Its evidence basis is the P-521 two-machine drill evidence plus the P-502 Leg G drill, not P-501 canary evidence. P-503 item text still says \"after P-501 ... 72h canary evidence\"; this decision supersedes that sentence.\nRelated: D-170, D-158, P-501, P-502, P-503","date":"2026-10-06","itemRefs":["P-501","P-402","P-404","P-308","P-503","P-401","P-502","P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":2233},{"id":"D-174","title":"D-166 census may cover the ORIGINAL signed log's latest complete snapshot set + tail (the producer's exact input) instead of all 8M blocks; fail-closed conditions","body":"Date: 2026-10-06\nL3 GO-reviewer ruling (su-3ecaf532, WI-10004684), answering f42's 2026-10-06T07:48Z messages coord-send-ccd689a7… and coord-send-1fe619c8… (WI-10004339). Fail-closed.\n\nMeasured by f42 and not yet re-derived by me: the default release selection is 1 core, length 8060061, authenticated head byteLength 184693843466, head signature verified. Code I read at staging: the census exporter (seed-provider-corestore.ts) folds from block 0 and reports sourceBlocksRead = sourceLength. print-gitleaks-findings.py:2172 requires sourceBlocksRead == sourceLength. findLatestCompleteSnapshot (read-merge.ts:1125) scans backward and verifies the whole set span [coversUpTo, coversUpTo+chunkCount); a seeded fold then reads only [seedIndex, length). produceFilteredSnapshotIntoLog (log-snapshot.ts:2133) seeds from it.\n\nRuling: YES. The D-166 census, and the GO re-derivation under D-164 G5 / D-166(3), may take as \"the frozen inputs\" the producer's exact input, i.e. the latest complete snapshot set of the ORIGINAL signed log plus its tail. Reading blocks before the snapshot set is not required. Why: the safety property is about what ships, and the shipped seed is a function of that span alone. A census over the same span is an exact accounting of shipped occurrences; a census over all 8M blocks would count superseded rows that never ship. ALL of these must hold:\n1. Same input, bound once. The census and the producer use the same maintained functions at the same frozen blobs: findLatestCompleteSnapshotDetailed plus the snapshot-seeded fold, never a reimplementation. Both run against the same core key, sourceLength and verified signed head. Both record identical seedIndex, coversUpTo, chunkCount and a digest of the snapshot set. If the producer folds from 0 (no complete set in the window), the census also folds from 0.\n2. Authenticated originals only. Every block read, including every snapshot chunk, comes from the original signed log, is verified against the bound head (Merkle/signature), and is decrypted with its original envelope AEAD. Projected, rewritten or partially copied storage is not a census input.\n3. Exact guard, not a loosened one. The Python guard and the exporter assert sourceBlocksRead == the declared span's block count. The manifest carries the declared span (seedIndex, coversUpTo, chunkCount, sourceLength) and the check is an equality. A >= check, or any omission without a declaration, refuses.\n4. Winner reconciliation. The census lists every winning (table, hbKey) of the seeded fold with its privacyProjection disposition. The set of rows the producer actually emitted must equal the census set with disposition carry or redact, compared key for key. A produced row with no census entry, or vice versa, is NO-GO.\n5. Honest reporting. The manifest and every GO record state coverage = complete-snapshot-set + tail, with omittedPrefixBlocks = seedIndex and the blocks actually read. They never claim that all 8,060,061 blocks were read. The D-165/D-166(2d) counts are restated over this span: authenticated-original plus redacted-reattested or dropped.\n6. Prefix never ships. No shipped artifact (installers, seed, manifest, bundled docs, any corestore copy) contains any block or value from before the span except through the seeded fold. If any artifact ships original-log storage, this ruling does not cover that artifact; the full-log census applies to it.\n7. Falsifiability, in the real test suite (Vitest, beside seed-provider-corestore.test.ts). On a fixture log: (a) census-from-span and census-from-0 produce identical winner sets and dispositions; (b) a sentinel value present only in a superseded prefix row is absent from both outputs and is reported as prefix-omitted; (c) a torn newest set falls back to the earlier complete set, or to 0, and the guard stays exact; (d) a mismatch between declared span and blocks read makes the guard refuse.\n8. Unchanged: G4 full key scans on the exact shipped installers, D-166(2) redaction conditions, D-165, Git history, and every other G1-G6 check. This ruling changes census scope only. It accepts no seed, candidate or guard change by itself.\nGO re-derives the snapshot-set selection, span bounds and winner reconciliation independently from the frozen inputs. Attested JSON alone is not evidence.\nRelated: D-166, D-165, D-164, P-521","date":"2026-10-06","itemRefs":["P-521"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":2242},{"id":"D-175","title":"D-174 clarification: frozen-code identity pinned by blobs + clean commit + lockfile (no per-file transitive hash); superseded rows need signed-proof verification, not an AEAD pass","body":"Date: 2026-10-06\nL3 GO-reviewer clarification (su-3ecaf532, WI-10004684), answering f42 coord-send-1cb425010e… and coord-send-fd1efac92e… (WI-10006530). Fail-closed. Supersedes the literal reading of D-174(1) and D-174(2) only where stated below.\n\nQ1. Frozen-blob identity (D-174(1)). Binding the SHA256 of the selector, fold, provider and producer source blobs is necessary but not sufficient. A per-file hash of the whole transitive graph is NOT required. Pin the graph by reference instead. ALL of these must hold, identically, in the census record and the producer record:\n a. The direct blobs, with sha256 and repo path: read-merge.ts (findLatestCompleteSnapshotDetailed), the extracted shared fold, seed-provider-corestore.ts, and log-snapshot.ts (produceFilteredSnapshotIntoLog).\n b. The 40-char source commit both ran from, from a clean checkout of that commit (gitDirty=false, an isolated root like the release cut). The commit pins every first-party transitive import.\n c. The package-lock.json sha256, with installed third-party packages integrity-matched to that lock (npm ci or equivalent), plus the node version. This pins hypercore, hyperbee, the crypto libraries and the rest of the third-party graph.\n d. Execution from those bytes. A compiled bundle or stale runtime whose loaded module does not match (a) refuses, as f42 proposed.\n If (a)-(d) differ between census and producer, refuse. Only runs at the final release mainSha count as GO evidence; runs at the current preparation head do not.\n\nQ2. Original-span AEAD (D-174(2)). An explicit AEAD pass over superseded sealed rows is NOT required. The signed block proofs already authenticate the ciphertext bytes of every block, and a superseded row's plaintext reaches no shipped artifact. ALL of these must hold:\n a. Every block in the declared span, whether superseded, winning or a snapshot chunk, has its Hypercore proof verified against the bound signed head. A local disk read without a proof does not count.\n b. Every winning row is AEAD-opened with its original envelope. An AEAD failure on a winner is NO-GO; it is never skipped or dropped silently.\n c. Winner selection may use only proof-verified cleartext structure. If the fold reads any SEALED field of a row to decide winners, deletions or order, that row is AEAD-opened too.\n d. The manifest reports the proof-verified block count, the AEAD-opened row count and the unopened superseded row count, so the omission is visible.\nD-174(3)-(8) are unchanged. GO re-derives (Q1 a-d) and (Q2 a-d) independently from the frozen inputs.\nRelated: D-174, D-166, D-164","date":"2026-10-06","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":2260},{"id":"D-176","title":"D-174(2) admits a complete proof-built private replica of the declared span (head equality, proof-only admission, exact inventory, read-time audit); arbitrary storage copies stay excluded","body":"Date: 2026-10-06\nL3 GO-reviewer ruling (su-3ecaf532, WI-10004684), answering f42 coord-send-d45dd4c50f… and coord-send-19fa72f41c… (WI-10006530). Fail-closed.\n\nQuestion: does D-174(2)'s exclusion of \"partially copied storage\" forbid a fresh private replica built by applying each ORIGINAL signed block proof and head proof for [seedIndex, length)?\n\nRuling: NO. Such a replica is admissible as census and producer input. D-174(2) excludes storage copied outside the log's own authentication, e.g. the cancelled arbitrary RocksDB column-family copy, which remains inadmissible. The identity of \"the original signed log\" is its key, length, tree root and signature, not the storage medium. A replica whose every block entered through a verified proof against that exact signed head is that log, restricted to the declared span. ALL of these must hold:\n a. Head equality. The replica's public key, length (= bound sourceLength), tree root hash and signature are byte-equal to the bound original head, and the signature verifies under the original key inside the replica.\n b. Proof-only admission. Every block in [seedIndex, length) enters the replica only through the maintained Hypercore proof-verification path against that head. Blocks are original ciphertext bytes; nothing is raw-inserted or rewritten.\n c. Exact inventory. The build emits a proof inventory: the span bounds, a count equal to length - seedIndex, and a digest over (index, block hash) for the whole span. It has no gaps and no blocks before seedIndex. The census and producer records both cite the same inventory digest.\n d. One capture. Everything comes from a single point-in-time original handle at the bound length. Any head drift during capture aborts the build; heads are never mixed.\n e. Integrity at read time. Satisfies D-175 Q2(a) by equivalence: immediately before the census reads and before the producer reads, a full audit recomputes every span block hash against the replica's tree up to the bound signed root, with zero mismatches. A replica that changed after it was built must fail this.\n f. Custody. The replica holds no writer or signing secret, never ships (D-174(6)), and is kept private and read-only until GO completes, so GO can re-verify (a), (c) and (e) itself.\nD-174(1),(3)-(8) and D-175 are unchanged. GO re-derives (a)-(e) independently.\nRelated: D-174, D-175, D-166","date":"2026-10-06","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":2279},{"id":"D-177","title":"D-175 Q1(c) is met by the committed lock (input-manifest digest) + version match + D-151(a)-style content check on the security-relevant subset + generation tree fingerprint; npm hidden .package-lock.json not required","body":"Date: 2026-10-06\nL3 GO-reviewer clarification of D-175 Q1(c) (su-3ecaf532, WI-10004684), answering f42 coord-send-6c6a50204c… (2026-10-06 11:08Z, WI-10004339). Fail-closed.\n\nf42's report: the frozen execution failed with ENOENT on node_modules/.package-lock.json, because dependency_generation_prune_ephemeral drops it from published generations. I read apps/operator/bin/release/dependency-generation.sh at staging. dependency_generation_tree_fingerprint deliberately excludes ./.package-lock.json, and dependency_generation_input_manifest_ref digests the COMMITTED package-lock.json / npm-shrinkwrap.json blobs at a git ref.\n\nRuling: D-175 Q1(c) does NOT require npm's hidden .package-lock.json. \"The package-lock.json sha256\" means the committed lockfile(s) at the bound commit. Do not resurrect the hidden lock, regenerate it, or build a new capture surface for it; that would be a third evidence surface beside two vetted ones. Satisfy Q1(c) with the existing surfaces. ALL of these must hold, identically, in the census and producer records:\n 1. Lock identity. Record the dependency_generation_input_manifest_ref digest at the bound 40-char commit. It must equal the input-manifest key of the dependency generation actually executed.\n 2. Version match. For every installed package under that generation's node_modules, the package.json name and version equal the committed lock entry for the same path. An installed package with no lock entry, or a non-optional lock entry missing from the tree, refuses.\n 3. Content integrity for the security-relevant subset, using the D-151(a) pattern. For hypercore, hyperbee, hypercore-crypto, the sodium bindings, and whichever package implements the envelope AEAD: fetch the tarball at the lock's resolved URL, require its sha512 to equal the lock integrity, and require every executed file's sha256 to equal the same path in that tarball. The rest of the third-party graph is covered by 2 plus 4.\n 4. No drift. dependency_generation_tree_fingerprint recomputed immediately before the census run and before the producer run equals the value recorded at publication.\n 5. Node version recorded, as in D-175.\nIf f42 still captures the original hidden lock, it is supplementary only. It must be the exact bytes npm wrote at install time, hashed then, and it never substitutes for 2-4. GO re-derives 1-4 independently.\nRelated: D-175, D-151, D-174","date":"2026-10-06","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":2295},{"id":"D-178","title":"D-177(2): npm reify-leftover dirs (.<name>-<8 alnum>) inside scopes are not installed packages; narrow match, reported, unreachable, drift-covered, never shipped","body":"Date: 2026-10-06\nL3 GO-reviewer clarification of D-177 clause 2 (su-3ecaf532, WI-10004684), answering f42 coord-send-cba93f3025… (2026-10-06 18:52Z, WI-10006840). Fail-closed.\n\nf42 reports: node_modules/@adobe/.css-tools-kD9rOVxL carries package.json @adobe/css-tools 4.4.4 with no lock entry, and is present in published generation 808 and frozen 9074. It has the shape of an npm reify leftover: a renamed old package directory, .<name>-<random>, that an install left behind. Node's resolver cannot reach it by package specifier. scripts/check-partial-install.mjs:154/165 already skips dot-prefixed entries at root and in scope directories.\n\nRuling: such directories do NOT count as installed packages for D-177(2). The symmetric scoped filter is correct, but only within these bounds, ALL required:\n a. Narrow match. Exclude only dot-prefixed names: at the node_modules root, the known tooling entries (.bin, .package-lock.json, .cache, .vite and similar); inside a scope, only entries matching npm's leftover shape ^\\.[^/]+-[A-Za-z0-9]{8}$. Any other dot-prefixed entry inside a scope refuses, and every normal (non-dot) scoped or unscoped package without a lock entry still refuses. f42's planned tests for unlocked normal scoped packages and hidden-byte drift are required.\n b. Reported, not silent. The inventory lists every excluded entry with its path, its package.json name and version, and a count. The census and producer records carry the same list.\n c. Unreachable. No module the census or producer actually loads resolves into an excluded directory, and no symlink in the generation targets one. Check it against the loaded-module path list of both runs.\n d. Drift still covered. D-177(4) tree-fingerprint equality applies to these bytes as to everything else.\n e. Never shipped. An excluded directory has no lock binding, so it cannot satisfy D-151(a). If its path or contents appear in any shipped artifact, that is NO-GO under D-164 G2/G4.\nGO re-derives (a)-(e) independently.\nRelated: D-177, D-175, D-151, D-164","date":"2026-10-06","itemRefs":[],"affects":[],"lineNumber":2310},{"id":"D-179","title":"Decouple the remaining P2P plan from the 0.0.29 publication: P-521 and the GO run on a private, clean drill candidate","body":"Date: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [owner:Avi 2026-10-06 directive #1492, typed: \"is there any way we can make the remaining p2p work not dependant on the next release? It's holding it up a lot\"; this repeats Avi's 2026-10-02T23:11Z request recorded in D-152]. Ruling by su-32c78573 (plan driver WI-2037678, P-521 holder WI-2144482) under AUTO.\n\nContext: the P-521 item text requires \"one clean reproducible candidate\", not a published release. The tie to exact 0.0.28/0.0.29 published bytes came from agent rulings (D-090, D-152 'STAYS TIED' list, D-153). 0.0.29 is now blocked on two independent paths: the green gate (main held ~28h, round 8 of repairs) and publication-only seed census safeguards (D-166 through D-178). Neither path tests P2P behaviour.\n\nRuling:\n1. Supersedes D-090 and D-152's 'STAYS TIED TO EXACT BYTES' list for P-521, P-401, P-502, P-503, P-403 and P-404. Evidence for those items may come from a PRIVATE DRILL CANDIDATE.\n2. A private drill candidate is built with the maintained build scripts from one clean commit (no gitDirty; provenance and sha recorded in the manifest). It is installed on the physical rig and NEVER published. Green main is NOT required; D-169's green-main rule governs the 0.0.29 PUBLICATION cut only.\n3. Default source: repair head 13d1d7852e26a85f7df460853f5c7875162aac12. Every test suite passed there and only lint legs were red; it contains all 0.0.29 source and already has shakedown build prep. The builder may move to a later clean commit only to pick up a needed P2P fix, and must record why.\n4. The publication-only steps (the D-166..D-178 seed census/redaction, the final-installer secret rescan D-142/D-147, tagging, full-history replacement) do NOT apply to the drill candidate. They stay on the 0.0.29 publication lane (WI-10004339).\n5. P-521 journeys, the P521-HARDENED-ACCEPTANCE rows and the P-401 independent GO are recorded against the drill candidate's sha and manifest. Source: [self-imposed engineering ruling by the D-230 driver su-def821c4 under AUTO, derived from recorded owner authority D-112]. This is NOT a new owner ruling.\n\nMeasured (WI-6554700010011908): the D-224 candidate (faa5abc1 / build 2018b667) has no hive seed in either Server artifact. The Linux Server .deb was built with the vm-release profile, which excludes seed/** by design. The Mac Server was built from a clean checkout where src-tauri/seed/ (gitignored) was absent, and SKIP_SEED_CUT=1 only warned. As a result P-521 J8 linux offline-restore failed by construction: the pot cannot appear offline and the boot ends at 'join awaiting GitHub sign-in'.\n\nThe open owner question conv-mv7q8fsw offered three routes: (a) drop offline-restore from 0.0.26 scope, (b) rebuild only the Mac Server seeded, (c) rebuild every role seeded. Recorded authority already decides most of it:\n- D-112 [owner:Avi 2026-10-01, verbatim, directive #1113]: \"0.0.26 Server ships WITH the full-history dogfood seed\", and \"the installer run (which needs a seeded pot) run on r6, and GO binds to r6\". Route (a) is out. It contradicts D-112 item 5 and D-208.\n2. Route (b) is insufficient. J8 failed on the LINUX Server, so a Mac-only rebuild cannot fix it.\n3. Route (c) is narrowed to Server roles only: rebuild the Linux Server and the Mac Server with the Tower-cut seed staged (bin/ensure-release-seed.sh). The D-224 GUI artifacts (Linux GUI .deb, Mac GUI) stand per D-208; rebuild them only if a shared-version or binding check forces it.\n4. The Linux Server cannot use the vm-release profile for this candidate, because that profile excludes seed/** and the owner's D-112 outranks the agent-derived vm-release choice (D-191/D-210/D-216). The Linux Server is built with the seed-carrying dogfood profile. Its vm-release-only obligations (trust toolchain, prompt prune per WI-10007067) are re-checked on the rebuilt artifact. Any obligation that cannot hold is filed, never silently dropped.\n5. Every Server producer now refuses a release-audited seedless build (release_seed_guard: WI-6554700010012075 + WI-6554700010012186), so the rebuild cannot repeat the D-224 failure silently.\n6. After the rebuild: J8 is re-run on the new Server, then the remaining P-521 journeys, then P-401 GO, which binds to the rebuilt candidate.\n\nOwner override: conv-mv7q8fsw stays open. Source: [self-imposed engineering ruling by the D-230 driver su-def821c4 under AUTO, implementing D-234 route (c) under D-112]. This is NOT an owner ruling.\n\nMeasured (WI-6554700010012467, 09:50Z): the seeded Linux Server cannot be one Debian package. An ar member's size field is 10 decimal digits, so no .deb member may exceed 9,999,999,999 bytes. The 6cbac6c0 dogfood Server payload is 14.91G uncompressed: seed 8.21G (full-history super.bundle 5.32G, submodule bundles 0.93G, corestore 1.96G) + sidecar 6.45G (HF ONNX models 3.43G, source.tar.zst 1.30G). Its xz data member is 11,290,740,252 bytes, 13% over the cap. The repack guard refused with exit 12, so nothing corrupt was produced. There is no duplication in the payload (listing: d235-linux-server-data-listing.txt in the D-235 bank). My earlier ~9.58G projection was wrong: it used the vm-release profile's 1.48G deb as the unseeded baseline, but D-234 item 4 moved this Server to the dogfood profile, whose sidecar alone compresses to about 3.2G.\n\nRuling:\n1. The Linux Server's seed ships as a companion package papercusp-server-seed (Architecture: all, same Version). It owns exactly usr/lib/Papercusp Server/seed/**, the path main.rs already reads (<parent-of-sidecar>/seed). No runtime change. No maintainer script references the seed.\n2. papercusp-server gains 'Recommends: papercusp-server-seed' (unversioned: the seed is only consumed at first boot, and a server upgrade must not demand a matching seed). Without the companion the Server cold-joins, as it does today when no seed is present.\n3. The split is a maintained post-build packaging step in papercusp-desktop/bin (with node tests), applied to the 6cbac6c0 bundle output and then passed through the maintained repack-deb-xz.sh (dedupe, xz, scrub check, re-sign). Like the WI-6554700010012467 repack delta, it is a packaging-tool delta and does not change the compiled build identity of D-235 item 2. The nomination D-NNN cites both deltas.\n4. Install for offline restore (J8 and docs): apt install both files. J8 installs both. The Tauri updater keeps serving only papercusp-server.\n5. The Mac Server is unaffected: a DMG/UDIF has no 10G member cap, so the seed stays inside the .app.\n6. Headroom: the seed package is about 8.1G against a 9.99G cap (about 19% margin). A future seed past the cap needs the seed itself split across members/packages. That is filed as a follow-up, not solved now.\n7. Future Server producers apply the same split, so a seeded Linux Server can never again be emitted as an over-cap single package.\nOwner override: conv-mv7q8fsw remains the override channel for D-234 scope.\nRelated: P-521, P-401, D-234, D-235","date":"2026-10-14","itemRefs":["P-521","P-401"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":2809},{"id":"D-237","title":"0.0.26 ships from the 6cbac6c0 bank without the Linux Server boot-start helper; the packaging fix (WI-6554700010012562) rides 0.0.27","body":"Date: 2026-10-14\nContext: WI-6554700010012562 (su-94154) found that no packaged Server has ever shipped src-tauri/systemd/enable-boot-start.sh (committed 2026-08-28 for WI-479556, never referenced by any tauri*.json). On a headless host with no login session and no linger, papercusp-server.service is not running after a reboot. su-94154's fix (both Server overlays map /usr/sbin/papercusp-server-enable-boot-start) is in the shared tree as of ~10:30Z 2026-10-14, AFTER the 0.0.26 bank source 6cbac6c0.\n\nRuling [self, AUTO under owner directive #1842]: the 0.0.26 candidate stays the D-234/D-235 seeded bank built from 6cbac6c0. It does NOT carry the helper.\n\nWhy: (1) not a regression; every released Server has the same gap, so 0.0.26 is no worse than 0.0.25. (2) Including it means rebuilding at least the Linux Server role from a newer SHA (about 2.5h for seed cut + build, then the D-236 split + repack), which either mixes source SHAs across roles in one manifest or restarts the all-roles rebuild D-234 required, and invalidates evidence already banked. (3) The helper is two commands, so 0.0.26 users have an exact manual equivalent.\n\nObligations: (a) 0.0.26 release notes carry a known-issue line: on a headless Linux Server host run `sudo loginctl enable-linger <user>` then, as that user, `systemctl --user enable --now papercusp-server.service`. (b) The Linux operations runbook must say the /usr/sbin/papercusp-server-enable-boot-start helper ships from 0.0.27, and give the manual equivalent for 0.0.26. (c) WI-6554700010012562's acceptance (dpkg -L lists the helper; reboot with no session yields a healthy operator) is checked on the 0.0.27 candidate. (d) The D-236 seed splitter keeps /usr/sbin/* in the main papercusp-server package (it moves only seed paths), so the fix needs no splitter change.\n\nRevisit if: P-521 or a P-401 reviewer classifies headless reboot survival as a 0.0.26 ship criterion.","date":"2026-10-14","itemRefs":["P-521","P-401"],"affects":[],"lineNumber":2826},{"id":"D-238","title":"Nominate the D-235 seeded candidate 6cbac6c0 / build 617822ea (manifest 0a6ddd13) for P-521 acceptance; supersedes D-224 as THE candidate","body":"Date: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14\nSource: [self-imposed] driver nomination by su-def821c4 (driver WI-2037678, builder WI-6554700010011908, packaging WI-6554700010012560) under AUTO, executing D-234/D-235/D-236. One post-publication correction: the \"dispatched 09-01\" status noted below was subsequently UNDONE — the rig lane's owner-pause superseded the dispatch and both items were released un-executed; current truth is Phase 0 / P-001 above.\n\n**Fourteen weeks of p2p work, read end to end: every plan, item ledger, work-item, gate, and live session. The short answer — the stack got built and mostly verified; the program has been stuck for ~6 weeks on one thing: a live two-machine witness ceremony running on a fragile physical rig, with heavy custody bureaucracy around it.**\n\n- Progress: real — 12 plans terminal, 83% of head-plan items done\n- Tail: stalled — one serial rig bottleneck since mid-July\n- 2 owner decisions open (1 resolved 09-01); both unowned blockers dispatched (since released — see note above)\n\n**KPIs:** 70/84 items done across the three head plans (37/44, 26/31, 7/9; +4 deliberately dropped) · 10 plan items left, every one converging on the same live-witness path · 2 critical-path rig bugs with no owner at audit time · 7½ weeks = age of the oldest still-open live-drill item (P-302, opened 07-09).\n\n### Verdict — progressing or spinning? Both, in sequence.\n\nJune – early August was real, high-throughput progress. Twelve p2p plans reached a terminal state (voice/video channels, hive directory, performance suite, shared-hive release readiness, per-hive git + release gate, part-merge proof, publish guards…). Across the three head plans, 70 of 84 items are done with recorded evidence. The hive-git suites pass today at multiple shas (unit 181/181, integration 154/154 at the last recorded baseline; drill-guard and release-contract tests green again tonight), and the physical-drill suite was 51/51 at the last verified boundary. This is not a codebase going in circles.\n\nSince mid-July, the tail has been a convoy. Everything that remains is some form of \"run the live cross-machine witness and sign the result\" — and it all funnels through one serial bottleneck: the two-machine rig (tower + Mac VM), guarded by a fail-closed custody gate (p008:vm-rig-custody-safe) that demanded a controlled repair of the 84f7 seed core plus three consecutive all-green tower/VM/probe samples before any witness may run. The rig keeps breaking in new ways, each break spawns recovery work and custody rulings, the tree moves on, and the July evidence goes stale — forcing re-validation waves (that is what Phase 5 and Phase 6 of the release plan are). That loop is the \"spinning,\" and it continues until the bottleneck itself is attacked. The tower federation storm is NOT primarily a rejoin effect: it is the **nightly release seed cut**, recurring daily at 07:00Z (`bin/release-local.sh <ver> nightly` → `cut-seed-quiesced.sh:106` → `cut-seed-cli --workspace-id`, no `--no-force-backfill`). Confirmed by su-0300e: their 07:03–07:15Z P-004 sample ran no cut.\n\n**Mechanism.** `backfillLocalState` exists to rescue rows that predate the capture trigger and so never fired it — that condition is `fed_ts IS NULL`. The enqueue SELECTs never expressed it; they selected every local row. So the per-target `backfill_done` marker was the ONLY idempotence guard, and `force` bypasses exactly that marker. `force` therefore meant \"re-enqueue the entire projection\". It also skips `markTargetDone`, so nothing records the sweep and every forced run repeats it in full. cut-seed-cli passes `force:true, maxOpsPerAuthor:0` — the latter sets the per-author budget to Infinity, and `force` also skips the 1000-row bail cap (gated on `!opts.force`). Every guard is off at once.\n\n**Measured 2026-09-02** (live corpus, old predicate vs new): engineer_issues 149,372→0 · harness_plans 1,625→0 · harness_features_consolidated 1,238→0 · plan_item_assignments 98→0 · pot_members 2→0. **152,335 rows re-enqueued per nightly cut, of which 0 genuinely needed it.** The running cut has been blocked since 07:06Z logging `[cut-seed] waiting for the operator to drain N outbox row(s)` every 5s — waiting on the backlog it created. That backlog is why coordination rows federate ~6h late.\n\n**DECISION — the fix goes in `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/backfill-local-state.ts`, at the predicate.** Add the missing `fed_ts IS NULL` condition to both enqueue paths and both candidate counts, plus an explicit `resyncFederated` option for a deliberate re-anchor. Consequences other lanes must follow:\n\n1. **Do NOT fix this by passing `--no-force-backfill`** in the release step. That flag makes the marker authoritative, and the marker is dated 2026-06-25 — it would skip engineer_issues wholesale. It trades a flood for a staleness risk and leaves the defect armed for every other caller. The predicate fix makes `force` cheap and correct, so the release caller needs no change at all.\n2. **The release path stays untouched**, so the `apps/operator/lib/release/**` human policy gate (D-003) does not apply to this fix. That gate is why EI-12727 — the same defect, filed 2026-07-15 from the corestore-ratchet angle — was parked `needs-human` on 2026-08-21. It was parked for the wrong path; the defect is in operator-core, which is not gated.\n3. **Seed completeness is preserved.** Genuinely-unfederated rows are still enqueued, which is the constraint EI-12727's reviewer flagged as non-negotiable.\n4. **EI-12727 is the same defect and should close against this landing**, not separately. The private git seed is encrypted at rest, and its key arrives only post-admission, so that store is DEFERRED offline by design. The hive (pot) itself comes from the online join. An empty hive list on a fresh offline install is therefore designed behaviour, not a product defect.\n\nRULING (amends D-083 item 1, D-084): the installer row's 'offline restore' leg is redefined as OFFLINE SEED RESTORE. It passes when, on the egress-denied VM: (1) the installed seed manifest and stores are byte-identical to the .deb (already measured in run 7); and (2) the first-boot pre-join restore actually ran. The corestore store must report restored (not cold-path/ran:false), and the git store must report deferred-awaiting-key, which is the expected outcome. Read both from the sidecar's restore outcome / log, not inferred. If a leg (2) outcome is not observable in the installed build, the leg records UNMEASURED for (2), with the reason. It must never record PASS by inference. A hive appearing in pot:list needs an online authenticated join, and stays in the Discovery/join row per D-083. The leg name in the evidence changes so no reader mistakes it for a hive-restore claim. The row closes per D-085 on a run that passes this leg plus the other 11.\n\nNot chosen: (B) dropping the leg, because it would lose a real offline check of the seed path. (C) filing a product bug, because the design memo explicitly puts hive creation after the join.\n\n### D-088 — SUPERSEDES D-087: the installer offline-restore leg keeps its original meaning (the dogfood pot appears offline) and is measured after a bounded wait\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. su-3ee17ad9 [self-imposed ruling, AUTO under owner #801]. Evidence: the private packet gitleaks-focus/classification-review-packet-safe.json, source d740fc38, desktop gitlink c864f7a1]\n\nThe residuals after all 18 content segments were authenticated and plaintext-scanned: (A) one curl-auth-user plaintext finding with digest a1fa2f79…, in segment-000099 and segment-000101 (the same content twice). It is a correct historical loopback Kasm credential from the WI-1099257 desktop-suite evidence. (B) 62 source-scan findings in segment-000107, all from the hive-epoch-keys table. Each is an 80-byte libsodium crypto_box_seal envelope (a 32-byte epoch key plus 48 bytes of overhead) produced by hive-epoch-crypto-impl.ts:97. The rows cover epochs 0-1, which already ship in epoch-keys.json, sealed to 33 recipient public keys.\n\nRuling A: regenerate. The finding is a correct credential, and under D-112 and the 14:40Z ruling a plaintext credential is never allowlisted. Loopback scope, age, and the fact that it sits in an issue comment do not change that. The \"documented public dummy\" class is refused: the value worked, so it is not a dummy. Required steps: (1) redact the credential at its DB source, the WI-1099257 content or comment row, using a documented verb with an audit row; (2) rotate the Kasm credential if any Kasm instance still accepts it; (3) regenerate the seed; (4) rescan the new seed in full, with a proof that this exact digest is absent. Do not hand-edit segment blobs.\n\nRuling B: the envelopes get the D-140 exact-digest exemption under a new class, recipient-sealed-epoch-key-envelope. Reasoning: a crypto_box_seal envelope is ciphertext that the public cannot open. Its only possible plaintext is 32 bytes, and the producer writes only epoch keys, which already ship. Opening one needs a recipient X25519 secret key, derived from a member's ed25519 identity key (impl.ts:59). Each exempted digest must have a fail-closed proof of four things: (1) the exact match decodes to an 80-byte value that equals a hive-epoch-keys envelope field in the same blob; (2) the row's epoch is in epoch-keys.json and its recipient public key is in the 33-key population; (3) a scan of the candidate artifact (seed and bundle) finds no ed25519 or X25519 secret key and no identity keystore, and that scan is checked by a positive control (a planted secret key must be detected); (4) the standard D-141 negative controls. If proof (3) cannot be produced, fall back to regenerating the seed without the envelope rows, but only after showing the importer does not require them. Because Ruling A forces a regeneration anyway, the envelope digests must be re-derived on the regenerated seed; the exemption binds the new exact digests and blob identity.\n\nUnchanged: no credential allowlist; no blob, path, line, or native-fingerprint suppression (D-140/D-141); D-125 source and tag immutability (d740/c864 stay frozen, and regenerating the seed is not a source change); a full Git history is still required. Every provisional class stays unapproved until the L3 GO reviewer (WI-10004684) audits the safe proofs independently. This ruling authorizes no collection, build, GO, or publication beyond the steps above.\nRelated: P-521\n\n### D-143 — 0.0.28 seed residue: sanitize the Kasm fixture password and regenerate the seed; accept the 62 sealed epoch-key envelopes under a structural, fail-closed class\nDate: 2026-10-02\nRATIFIES D-142 + REDACTION PATH. Honest reporting. The manifest and every GO record state coverage = complete-snapshot-set + tail, with omittedPrefixBlocks = seedIndex and the blocks actually read. No shipped artifact (installers, seed, manifest, bundled docs, any corestore copy) contains any block or value from before the span except through the seeded fold. Falsifiability, in the real test suite (Vitest, beside seed-provider-corestore.test.ts). On a fixture log: (a) census-from-span and census-from-0 produce identical winner sets and dispositions; (b) a sentinel value present only in a superseded prefix row is absent from both outputs and is reported as prefix-omitted; (c) a torn newest set falls back to the earlier complete set, or to 0, and the guard stays exact; (d) a mismatch between declared span and blocks read makes the guard refuse.\n8. Attested JSON alone is not evidence.\nRelated: D-166, D-165, D-164, P-521\n\n### D-175 — D-174 clarification: frozen-code identity pinned by blobs + clean commit + lockfile (no per-file transitive hash); superseded rows need signed-proof verification, not an AEAD pass\nDate: 2026-10-06\nL3 GO-reviewer clarification (su-3ecaf532, WI-10004684), answering f42 coord-send-1cb425010e… and coord-send-fd1efac92e… (WI-10006530). The replica's public key, length (= bound sourceLength), tree root hash and signature are byte-equal to the bound original head, and the signature verifies under the original key inside the replica.\n b. Any head drift during capture aborts the build; heads are never mixed.\n e. Integrity at read time. Satisfies D-175 Q2(a) by equivalence: immediately before the census reads and before the producer reads, a full audit recomputes every span block hash against the replica's tree up to the bound signed root, with zero mismatches. It owns exactly usr/lib/Papercusp Server/seed/**, the path main.rs already reads (<parent-of-sidecar>/seed). No runtime change. No maintainer script references the seed.\n2. papercusp-server gains 'Recommends: papercusp-server-seed' (unversioned: the seed is only consumed at first boot, and a server upgrade must not demand a matching seed). Without the companion the Server cold-joins, as it does today when no seed is present.\n3. The split is a maintained post-build packaging step in papercusp-desktop/bin (with node tests), applied to the 6cbac6c0 bundle output and then passed through the maintained repack-deb-xz.sh (dedupe, xz, scrub check, re-sign). Like the WI-6554700010012467 repack delta, it is a packaging-tool delta and does not change the compiled build identity of D-235 item 2. The nomination D-NNN cites both deltas.\n4. Install for offline restore (J8 and docs): apt install both files. J8 installs both. The Tauri updater keeps serving only papercusp-server.\n5. The Mac Server is unaffected: a DMG/UDIF has no 10G member cap, so the seed stays inside the .app.\n6. Headroom: the seed package is about 8.1G against a 9.99G cap (about 19% margin).
